1	# Release Checklist
2	
3	**Title:** Release Checklist
4	**Version:** 2.4
5	**Owner:** Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)
6	**Last updated:** 2026-02-03
7	
8	**Summary:** This page walks through the ordered steps a maintainer follows before tagging a new build of accountsvc, from confirming the changelog and command help text are current through packaging the source distribution and posting release notes. It is meant to be read start to finish the first time a person runs a release, and skimmed as a reference afterward.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## Overview
13	
14	*Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*
15	
16	accountsvc ships as a plain source distribution — there is no compiled extension and no external dependency to pin, since the package only uses the standard library. That keeps the release mechanics simple, but the checklist still exists because small things get missed: a version marker left at the old number, a changelog entry with no date, a help text string that drifted from what the command actually prints, a console log line that no longer matches the format documented in `docs/console-log-format.md`.
17	
18	This page covers the full extent of the release process — version numbering, changelog conventions, the pre-release checklist itself, packaging the source distribution, and a running list of what shipped in each past version. Two sibling pages (`version-numbering.md` and `changelog-conventions.md`) go into more detail on their respective topics; this page gives the working summary a maintainer actually needs while running through a release.
19	
20	The range of a typical accountsvc release has stayed narrow for a while now. Looking back at the last several versions, almost everything that shipped falls into one of five buckets: documentation wording, packaging fixes, command help text, the console log line format, or speed. There has not been a release in over a year that changed anything outside those five areas, and this checklist is organized around that reality.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## Terminology
25	
26	*Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*
27	
28	- **Source distribution** — the single distributable file produced for a release; for accountsvc this is a gzip-compressed tarball containing the package directory, metadata, and non-code files needed to install it.
29	- **Version marker** — the short string inside the package that declares its current version number; this is the value that gets bumped before every release.
30	- **Console log format** — the fixed layout of lines the service and command line print to standard output and standard error, including the timestamp prefix and field order.
31	- **Help text** — the usage description printed when a command is run without arguments or with an unrecognized one; kept in a plain-text reference copy under `docs/`.
32	- **Changelog** — the top-level file recording what changed in each version, in reverse chronological order, one heading per version.
33	- **Release note** — a longer, prose-style writeup for a single version, distinct from its changelog entry, usually one page per version under `docs/release-notes/`.
34	- **Database file** — the local SQLite file the service reads and writes; the checklist only cares whether a fresh copy opens cleanly, not what it contains.
35	- **Loopback service** — the local-only HTTP service accountsvc runs; "loopback" here just means it only accepts connections from the same host.
36	- **Build output folder** — the local, disposable folder (`dist/`) where the source distribution file is produced before it is copied anywhere else.
37	- **Tag** — the git tag applied to the commit that a released version was built from, named after the version number.
38	
39	---
40	
41	## Version Numbering
42	
43	*Owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen) — summarized here by Release Engineering*
44	
45	accountsvc's version numbers are two parts, Major.Minor — for example, `2.2`, then `2.3`. The full reasoning for this scheme, including when a Major number changes versus a Minor one, lives on the "Version Numbering Scheme" page; this section is a working summary.
46	
47	In short:
48	
49	- A Minor bump (`2.2` → `2.3`) covers everything the last several releases have actually contained — documentation edits, packaging fixes, help text wording, console log format changes, and speed work.
50	- A Major bump (`1.x` → `2.0`) is reserved for anything that changes what a caller of the loopback service or the command line can rely on. There has not been a Major bump since `2.0` itself.
51	- Early versions of accountsvc (`v1.0.0` through `v1.2.0`) used a three-part number with a Patch component. Starting at `2.0`, the Patch component was dropped, since in practice it was never used for anything a Minor bump didn't already cover. Some older internal references still describe the three-part form as the standing convention — when in doubt, the version numbers actually used in `CHANGELOG.md` are the ones that matter.
52	
53	The version marker lives inside the package itself, not in a separate top-level file. Before packaging, open it in an editor and update the string by hand — there is no script that does this for you today, though one has been proposed more than once.
54	
55	A quick reference of what's shipped so far:
56	
57	| Version | Shipped | Numbering form |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| v1.0.0 | 2024-03-18 | three-part |
60	| v1.1.0 | 2024-07-05 | three-part |
61	| v1.2.0 | 2024-10-22 | three-part |
62	| 2.0 | 2025-02-11 | two-part |
63	| 2.1 | 2025-05-27 | two-part |
64	| 2.2 | 2025-09-15 | two-part |
65	| 2.3 | in progress | two-part (planned) |
66	
67	---
68	
69	## Changelog Conventions
70	
71	*Owner: Docs Guild (Sasha Perlman) — summarized here by Release Engineering*
72	
73	`CHANGELOG.md` sits at the repo root, one heading per version, most recent at the top. Entries below a version heading are grouped under one or more of: `Documentation`, `Packaging`, `Command help text`, `Console log format`, `Speed`. If a release genuinely doesn't touch one of those groups, that group heading is simply omitted for that version rather than left empty.
74	
75	A worked example, for a hypothetical `2.3` entry:
76	
77	```
78	## 2.3 — 2026-03-xx
79	
80	### Documentation
81	- Corrected the install steps in README.md to match the current folder layout.
82	
83	### Command help text
84	- Reworded the usage line for the account-lookup command so it wraps
85	  correctly in an 80-column terminal.
86	
87	### Speed
88	- Reduced repeated file opens during startup, shaving a small but
89	  measurable amount off cold-start time.
90	```
91	
92	A few conventions that are easy to get wrong on a first release:
93	
94	1. The version heading uses the bare number (`## 2.3`), not `v2.3`, matching the two-part scheme described above — except for the three older `v1.x.x` entries, which keep their original `v` prefix for continuity with their own release notes pages.
95	2. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`. If a release date isn't locked yet, the heading uses `2026-03-xx` as a stand-in and gets a real date filled in right before tagging — don't forget this step, it's the single most common thing left unfixed.
96	3. Each bullet is one sentence, written in the past tense, describing what changed rather than why.
97	4. Once a version's entry is added, its lines are not edited later. If something needs fixing after the fact, a new entry is added under the next version rather than changing an old one.
98	
99	For the complete entry grammar — heading levels, bullet punctuation, how to handle a version with nothing to report — see the "Changelog Entry Format" page, which is the newer, more precise sibling to the older "Changelog Conventions" page. The two occasionally disagree on small formatting points; the more recently updated one wins.
100	
101	---
102	
103	## Pre-Release Checklist
104	
105	*Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*
106	
107	Work through this list top to bottom. None of the steps are strictly automated today — a maintainer runs each one by hand and checks it off.
108	
109	1. Confirm every open item for the release is actually done. If something is still open, either finish it or pull it into the next version instead of shipping half of it.
110	2. Update the version marker inside the package to the new number.
111	3. Add the new heading to `CHANGELOG.md`, with a real date, grouped by category as described above.
112	4. Read through the command help text end to end and confirm it still matches what the command prints. If wording changed, update the reference copy at `docs/cli-help-text.md` to match.
113	5. Start the loopback service once, by hand, against a throwaway database file in a scratch folder, and confirm it starts and stops without printing anything unexpected to the console.
114	6. Compare a few lines of that console output against `docs/console-log-format.md`. If the format drifted — a field moved, the timestamp changed shape — either fix the format or update the documentation, and note which one happened in the changelog.
115	7. If the release includes speed work, note roughly what got faster and where, in plain language, in the changelog's `Speed` group.
116	8. Read through README.md and confirm the install steps and version number mentioned there (if any) are current.
117	9. Confirm `docs/release-notes/` has a draft page for the new version, even if it's short — see the Release Notes section below for the expected shape.
118	10. Walk through the packaging steps in the next section and confirm the resulting distribution file installs cleanly into a fresh, disposable folder.
119	11. Confirm the git working folder is clean — no unrelated edits sitting around — before tagging.
120	12. Get a second set of eyes on the changelog entry and the release notes draft. This has historically been Sasha Perlman or Priya Nandakumar, whoever is around.
121	13. Tag and publish, per the next section.
122	14. Once published, come back and finish the Post-Release steps further down this page.
123	
124	A shorter view of the same list, organized by the five areas this checklist cares about:
125	
126	| Area | What to check |
127	|---|---|
128	| Documentation | README.md and docs/ pages match the current version and behavior |
129	| Packaging | Version marker updated; distribution file builds and installs cleanly |
130	| Command help text | Printed help matches the reference copy in docs/cli-help-text.md |
131	| Console log format | Console output matches docs/console-log-format.md |
132	| Speed | Any speed change is noted in plain language in the changelog |
133	
134	---
135	
136	## Packaging the Source Distribution
137	
138	*Owner: Core Services (Elliot Fenwick)*
139	
140	accountsvc has no compiled parts, so packaging is straightforward: build a source distribution, check its contents, and copy it somewhere internal people can get to it. The full detail on this — including what belongs in `MANIFEST.in` and how `pyproject.toml` is laid out — lives on the "Packaging the Source Distribution" page and its shorter sibling, "Source Distribution Notes."
141	
142	Before building, clear out any old build output so you're not looking at a stale file:
143	
144	```
145	rm -rf dist/
146	```
147	
148	Build the source distribution with the standard build tool:
149	
150	```
151	python -m build --sdist --outdir dist/
152	```
153	
154	This produces a single file, something like `dist/accountsvc-2.3.tar.gz`. List its contents and eyeball them — this catches the most common packaging mistake, a file that got added to the package directory but never added to `MANIFEST.in`, so it's silently missing from the distribution:
155	
156	```
157	tar -tzf dist/accountsvc-2.3.tar.gz | sort
158	```
159	
160	Compare that list against what's actually in `accountsvc/` on disk. If something is missing, add it to `MANIFEST.in` and build again.
161	
162	Next, confirm the packaged version installs and runs from a completely disposable location, not the working folder you've been editing in:
163	
164	```
165	mkdir /tmp/accountsvc-check
166	tar -xzf dist/accountsvc-2.3.tar.gz -C /tmp/accountsvc-check
167	```
168	
169	From inside that extracted folder, confirm the package can start against a fresh database file. Point it at a scratch path that doesn't exist yet, and confirm the file gets created without complaint:
170	
171	```
172	sqlite3 /tmp/accountsvc-check/scratch.db "PRAGMA quick_check;"
173	```
174	
175	That command just confirms the file opens cleanly as a valid database file — it isn't meant to say anything about what's stored inside it.
176	
177	Once the distribution file looks right, record a checksum alongside it, mostly so anyone copying it later can confirm they got a whole, unbroken copy:
178	
179	```
180	sha256sum dist/accountsvc-2.3.tar.gz > dist/accountsvc-2.3.tar.gz.sha256
181	```
182	
183	Copy both files to the internal file share (`\\files\releases\accountsvc\`) under a folder named after the version number. There is no automatic upload step for this today; it's a manual copy, and it's worth double-checking the folder name matches the version exactly, since a typo here has caused confusion more than once.
184	
185	A short script exists to wrap the build-and-check steps above — `scripts/build-sdist.sh` — but it's a convenience, not a requirement, and it doesn't replace reading the tarball listing yourself.
186	
187	---
188	
189	## Tagging and Publishing the Release
190	
191	*Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*
192	
193	Once the packaging checks above pass, tag the commit the release was built from:
194	
195	```
196	git tag -a 2.3 -m "accountsvc 2.3"
197	git push origin 2.3
198	```
199	
200	The tag name matches the version number exactly, with no leading `v` for anything `2.0` and later (the three early `v1.x.x` releases kept their `v` prefix, and their tags reflect that).
201	
202	After pushing the tag, update the copy of the release notes page for the new version under `docs/release-notes/` with its final content — including the actual date — and update this checklist's own header date only if this page itself changed during the release, which is uncommon.
203	
204	Post a short message in the team's internal channel with the version number, the tag, and a link to the release notes page. There is no separate publishing target beyond the internal file share described above; accountsvc is not published anywhere external.
205	
206	---
207	
208	## Post-Release Checklist
209	
210	*Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*
211	
212	- Confirm the tag actually landed (`git tag --list` from a clean clone, or check the internal git browser).
213	- Confirm the distribution file and its checksum are both present on the file share, in the correctly named folder.
214	- Confirm the release notes page for the new version is complete and dated, not left as a draft.
215	- If any console log copies were saved locally during the walkthrough in step 5 of the pre-release checklist, they can be cleared out of the scratch folder they were made in — there is no need to keep them.
216	- Open an item for whatever got pushed to the next version during step 1, so it doesn't quietly disappear.
217	- Note the release in the "Release Schedule" page if the date differs from what was originally planned there.
218	
219	---
220	
221	## Release Notes for Past Versions
222	
223	*Owner: Developer Experience (Priya Nandakumar), later versions by Platform Tools and Docs Guild*
224	
225	Every version release note gets its own page under `docs/release-notes/`. What follows is a short summary of each one shipped so far — the full writeups are the pages themselves, linked below in Related Pages.
226	
227	| Version | Shipped | Owner | What changed |
228	|---|---|---|---|
229	| v1.0.0 | 2024-03-18 | Priya Nandakumar | First numbered release. Documentation described initial install steps; command help text written for the first time. |
230	| v1.1.0 | 2024-07-05 | Priya Nandakumar | Packaging fix — a file referenced by `MANIFEST.in` had been renamed and was missing from the distribution; documentation updated to match. |
231	| v1.2.0 | 2024-10-22 | Mara Olsen | Console log lines gained a timestamp prefix; before this, lines had no time information at all, which made comparing local logs to anything else nearly impossible. |
232	| 2.0 | 2025-02-11 | Mara Olsen | Version numbering moved from three-part to two-part starting with this release; documentation across the repo updated to match; command help text reworded for clarity. |
233	| 2.1 | 2025-05-27 | Sasha Perlman | Console log format changed again — fields reordered so the timestamp comes first on every line, matching the convention used elsewhere internally. Documentation updated accordingly. |
234	| 2.2 | 2025-09-30 | Sasha Perlman | Speed work: startup was reworked to avoid several redundant file opens, measurably shortening cold start. No documentation or format changes beyond a short note in the changelog. |
235	
236	A few notes worth calling out on specific versions:
237	
238	**v1.2.0** is the version most people mean when they say "before we had timestamps" — anything printed by the console before this shipped can't be reliably ordered against anything else, since lines had no time information at all.
239	
240	**2.0** was a documentation-heavy release even though it also carried the numbering change; nearly every page under `docs/` got at least a small edit to reflect the new two-part version numbers.
241	
242	**2.2** is the most recent version actually shipped as of this page's last update. Work toward `2.3` is in progress and tracked on the "Release Schedule" page.
243	
244	---
245	
246	## Files and Paths Referenced
247	
248	- `accountsvc/` — the package directory itself; holds the version marker that gets updated before each release.
249	- `README.md` — repo-root readme with install steps and a short usage summary; kept in sync with the current version.
250	- `CHANGELOG.md` — repo-root changelog file, one heading per version, most recent first.
251	- `pyproject.toml` — packaging metadata used to build the source distribution.
252	- `MANIFEST.in` — lists non-code files that must be included when the distribution is built; the most common source of packaging misses when it falls out of date.
253	- `docs/release-notes/` — folder holding this checklist and one page per shipped version.
254	- `docs/console-log-format.md` — describes the expected console log line format; checked against real output during the pre-release checklist.
255	- `docs/cli-help-text.md` — reference copy of the current command-line help text, compared against the real printed help before each release.
256	- `scripts/build-sdist.sh` — convenience shell script wrapping the build and packaging-check steps.
257	- `dist/` — local, disposable build output folder where the source distribution file is produced; cleared before each build.
258	- `\\files\releases\accountsvc\` — internal file share where each version's distribution file and checksum are copied after tagging.
259	
260	---
261	
262	## Tools and Libraries
263	
264	| Tool / package | Version | Used for |
265	|---|---|---|
266	| Python | 3.11.9 | Interpreter used to build and run the package |
267	| build | 1.2.1 | Produces the source distribution file from pyproject.toml |
268	| git | 2.43.0 | Version control and tagging releases |
269	| sqlite3 (command-line shell) | 3.45.1 | Opens the database file to confirm it's valid after packaging |
270	| tar | GNU tar 1.35 | Lists and extracts the source distribution file for inspection |
271	| sha256sum | GNU coreutils 9.4 | Produces a checksum alongside each distribution file |
272	| shellcheck | 0.9.0 | Lints the shell scripts under scripts/ |
273	| pandoc | 3.1.11 | Renders changelog entries into a plain-text copy for the internal wiki export |
274	
275	---
276	
277	## Change Log
278	
279	*This section tracks changes to the checklist page itself, not to accountsvc.*
280	
281	- **2024-03-10 (v1.0)** — Initial checklist assembled by Priya Nandakumar, covering the steps used for the v1.0.0 release.
282	- **2024-07-01 (v1.2)** — Added a packaging verification step after the v1.1.0 distribution shipped with a missing file.
283	- **2024-10-18 (v1.5)** — Mara Olsen added the console log format check ahead of the v1.2.0 release, once timestamps were introduced.
284	- **2025-02-05 (v2.0)** — Rewrote the Version Numbering section to describe the move from three-part to two-part numbers for the 2.0 release; ownership of this section moved to Platform Tools.
285	- **2025-09-12 (v2.2)** — Sasha Perlman folded in the current five-area grouping (documentation, packaging, help text, console log format, speed) after realizing that's all recent releases had actually contained.
286	- **2026-01-30 (v2.4)** — Devon Ruiz restructured the page around the Pre-Release / Packaging / Post-Release split used today, and added the Files and Tools sections.
287	- **2026-02-03 (v2.4)** — Small wording fixes and an updated Release Notes table following the 2.2 release.
288	
289	---
290	
291	## Related Pages
292	
293	- Release Notes Folder Guide
294	- Version Numbering Scheme

# Release Checklist

**Title:** Release Checklist
**Version:** 2.4
**Owner:** Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)
**Last updated:** 2026-02-03

**Summary:** This page walks through the ordered steps a maintainer follows before tagging a new build of accountsvc, from confirming the changelog and command help text are current through packaging the source distribution and posting release notes. It is meant to be read start to finish the first time a person runs a release, and skimmed as a reference afterward.

---

## Overview

*Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*

accountsvc ships as a plain source distribution — there is no compiled extension and no external dependency to pin, since the package only uses the standard library. That keeps the release mechanics simple, but the checklist still exists because small things get missed: a version marker left at the old number, a changelog entry with no date, a help text string that drifted from what the command actually prints, a console log line that no longer matches the format documented in `docs/console-log-format.md`.

This page covers the full extent of the release process — version numbering, changelog conventions, the pre-release checklist itself, packaging the source distribution, and a running list of what shipped in each past version. Two sibling pages (`version-numbering.md` and `changelog-conventions.md`) go into more detail on their respective topics; this page gives the working summary a maintainer actually needs while running through a release.

The range of a typical accountsvc release has stayed narrow for a while now. Looking back at the last several versions, almost everything that shipped falls into one of five buckets: documentation wording, packaging fixes, command help text, the console log line format, or speed. There has not been a release in over a year that changed anything outside those five areas, and this checklist is organized around that reality.

---

## Terminology

*Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*

- **Source distribution** — the single distributable file produced for a release; for accountsvc this is a gzip-compressed tarball containing the package directory, metadata, and non-code files needed to install it.
- **Version marker** — the short string inside the package that declares its current version number; this is the value that gets bumped before every release.
- **Console log format** — the fixed layout of lines the service and command line print to standard output and standard error, including the timestamp prefix and field order.
- **Help text** — the usage description printed when a command is run without arguments or with an unrecognized one; kept in a plain-text reference copy under `docs/`.
- **Changelog** — the top-level file recording what changed in each version, in reverse chronological order, one heading per version.
- **Release note** — a longer, prose-style writeup for a single version, distinct from its changelog entry, usually one page per version under `docs/release-notes/`.
- **Database file** — the local SQLite file the service reads and writes; the checklist only cares whether a fresh copy opens cleanly, not what it contains.
- **Loopback service** — the local-only HTTP service accountsvc runs; "loopback" here just means it only accepts connections from the same host.
- **Build output folder** — the local, disposable folder (`dist/`) where the source distribution file is produced before it is copied anywhere else.
- **Tag** — the git tag applied to the commit that a released version was built from, named after the version number.

---

## Version Numbering

*Owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen) — summarized here by Release Engineering*

accountsvc's version numbers are two parts, Major.Minor — for example, `2.2`, then `2.3`. The full reasoning for this scheme, including when a Major number changes versus a Minor one, lives on the "Version Numbering Scheme" page; this section is a working summary.

In short:

- A Minor bump (`2.2` → `2.3`) covers everything the last several releases have actually contained — documentation edits, packaging fixes, help text wording, console log format changes, and speed work.
- A Major bump (`1.x` → `2.0`) is reserved for anything that changes what a caller of the loopback service or the command line can rely on. There has not been a Major bump since `2.0` itself.
- Early versions of accountsvc (`v1.0.0` through `v1.2.0`) used a three-part number with a Patch component. Starting at `2.0`, the Patch component was dropped, since in practice it was never used for anything a Minor bump didn't already cover. Some older internal references still describe the three-part form as the standing convention — when in doubt, the version numbers actually used in `CHANGELOG.md` are the ones that matter.

The version marker lives inside the package itself, not in a separate top-level file. Before packaging, open it in an editor and update the string by hand — there is no script that does this for you today, though one has been proposed more than once.

A quick reference of what's shipped so far:

| Version | Shipped | Numbering form |
|---|---|---|
| v1.0.0 | 2024-03-18 | three-part |
| v1.1.0 | 2024-07-05 | three-part |
| v1.2.0 | 2024-10-22 | three-part |
| 2.0 | 2025-02-11 | two-part |
| 2.1 | 2025-05-27 | two-part |
| 2.2 | 2025-09-15 | two-part |
| 2.3 | in progress | two-part (planned) |

---

## Changelog Conventions

*Owner: Docs Guild (Sasha Perlman) — summarized here by Release Engineering*

`CHANGELOG.md` sits at the repo root, one heading per version, most recent at the top. Entries below a version heading are grouped under one or more of: `Documentation`, `Packaging`, `Command help text`, `Console log format`, `Speed`. If a release genuinely doesn't touch one of those groups, that group heading is simply omitted for that version rather than left empty.

A worked example, for a hypothetical `2.3` entry:

```
## 2.3 — 2026-03-xx

### Documentation
- Corrected the install steps in README.md to match the current folder layout.

### Command help text
- Reworded the usage line for the account-lookup command so it wraps
  correctly in an 80-column terminal.

### Speed
- Reduced repeated file opens during startup, shaving a small but
  measurable amount off cold-start time.
```

A few conventions that are easy to get wrong on a first release:

1. The version heading uses the bare number (`## 2.3`), not `v2.3`, matching the two-part scheme described above — except for the three older `v1.x.x` entries, which keep their original `v` prefix for continuity with their own release notes pages.
2. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`. If a release date isn't locked yet, the heading uses `2026-03-xx` as a stand-in and gets a real date filled in right before tagging — don't forget this step, it's the single most common thing left unfixed.
3. Each bullet is one sentence, written in the past tense, describing what changed rather than why.
4. Once a version's entry is added, its lines are not edited later. If something needs fixing after the fact, a new entry is added under the next version rather than changing an old one.

For the complete entry grammar — heading levels, bullet punctuation, how to handle a version with nothing to report — see the "Changelog Entry Format" page, which is the newer, more precise sibling to the older "Changelog Conventions" page. The two occasionally disagree on small formatting points; the more recently updated one wins.

---

## Pre-Release Checklist

*Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*

Work through this list top to bottom. None of the steps are strictly automated today — a maintainer runs each one by hand and checks it off.

1. Confirm every open item for the release is actually done. If something is still open, either finish it or pull it into the next version instead of shipping half of it.
2. Update the version marker inside the package to the new number.
3. Add the new heading to `CHANGELOG.md`, with a real date, grouped by category as described above.
4. Read through the command help text end to end and confirm it still matches what the command prints. If wording changed, update the reference copy at `docs/cli-help-text.md` to match.
5. Start the loopback service once, by hand, against a throwaway database file in a scratch folder, and confirm it starts and stops without printing anything unexpected to the console.
6. Compare a few lines of that console output against `docs/console-log-format.md`. If the format drifted — a field moved, the timestamp changed shape — either fix the format or update the documentation, and note which one happened in the changelog.
7. If the release includes speed work, note roughly what got faster and where, in plain language, in the changelog's `Speed` group.
8. Read through README.md and confirm the install steps and version number mentioned there (if any) are current.
9. Confirm `docs/release-notes/` has a draft page for the new version, even if it's short — see the Release Notes section below for the expected shape.
10. Walk through the packaging steps in the next section and confirm the resulting distribution file installs cleanly into a fresh, disposable folder.
11. Confirm the git working folder is clean — no unrelated edits sitting around — before tagging.
12. Get a second set of eyes on the changelog entry and the release notes draft. This has historically been Sasha Perlman or Priya Nandakumar, whoever is around.
13. Tag and publish, per the next section.
14. Once published, come back and finish the Post-Release steps further down this page.

A shorter view of the same list, organized by the five areas this checklist cares about:

| Area | What to check |
|---|---|
| Documentation | README.md and docs/ pages match the current version and behavior |
| Packaging | Version marker updated; distribution file builds and installs cleanly |
| Command help text | Printed help matches the reference copy in docs/cli-help-text.md |
| Console log format | Console output matches docs/console-log-format.md |
| Speed | Any speed change is noted in plain language in the changelog |

---

## Packaging the Source Distribution

*Owner: Core Services (Elliot Fenwick)*

accountsvc has no compiled parts, so packaging is straightforward: build a source distribution, check its contents, and copy it somewhere internal people can get to it. The full detail on this — including what belongs in `MANIFEST.in` and how `pyproject.toml` is laid out — lives on the "Packaging the Source Distribution" page and its shorter sibling, "Source Distribution Notes."

Before building, clear out any old build output so you're not looking at a stale file:

```
rm -rf dist/
```

Build the source distribution with the standard build tool:

```
python -m build --sdist --outdir dist/
```

This produces a single file, something like `dist/accountsvc-2.3.tar.gz`. List its contents and eyeball them — this catches the most common packaging mistake, a file that got added to the package directory but never added to `MANIFEST.in`, so it's silently missing from the distribution:

```
tar -tzf dist/accountsvc-2.3.tar.gz | sort
```

Compare that list against what's actually in `accountsvc/` on disk. If something is missing, add it to `MANIFEST.in` and build again.

Next, confirm the packaged version installs and runs from a completely disposable location, not the working folder you've been editing in:

```
mkdir /tmp/accountsvc-check
tar -xzf dist/accountsvc-2.3.tar.gz -C /tmp/accountsvc-check
```

From inside that extracted folder, confirm the package can start against a fresh database file. Point it at a scratch path that doesn't exist yet, and confirm the file gets created without complaint:

```
sqlite3 /tmp/accountsvc-check/scratch.db "PRAGMA quick_check;"
```

That command just confirms the file opens cleanly as a valid database file — it isn't meant to say anything about what's stored inside it.

Once the distribution file looks right, record a checksum alongside it, mostly so anyone copying it later can confirm they got a whole, unbroken copy:

```
sha256sum dist/accountsvc-2.3.tar.gz > dist/accountsvc-2.3.tar.gz.sha256
```

Copy both files to the internal file share (`\\files\releases\accountsvc\`) under a folder named after the version number. There is no automatic upload step for this today; it's a manual copy, and it's worth double-checking the folder name matches the version exactly, since a typo here has caused confusion more than once.

A short script exists to wrap the build-and-check steps above — `scripts/build-sdist.sh` — but it's a convenience, not a requirement, and it doesn't replace reading the tarball listing yourself.

---

## Tagging and Publishing the Release

*Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*

Once the packaging checks above pass, tag the commit the release was built from:

```
git tag -a 2.3 -m "accountsvc 2.3"
git push origin 2.3
```

The tag name matches the version number exactly, with no leading `v` for anything `2.0` and later (the three early `v1.x.x` releases kept their `v` prefix, and their tags reflect that).

After pushing the tag, update the copy of the release notes page for the new version under `docs/release-notes/` with its final content — including the actual date — and update this checklist's own header date only if this page itself changed during the release, which is uncommon.

Post a short message in the team's internal channel with the version number, the tag, and a link to the release notes page. There is no separate publishing target beyond the internal file share described above; accountsvc is not published anywhere external.

---

## Post-Release Checklist

*Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*

- Confirm the tag actually landed (`git tag --list` from a clean clone, or check the internal git browser).
- Confirm the distribution file and its checksum are both present on the file share, in the correctly named folder.
- Confirm the release notes page for the new version is complete and dated, not left as a draft.
- If any console log copies were saved locally during the walkthrough in step 5 of the pre-release checklist, they can be cleared out of the scratch folder they were made in — there is no need to keep them.
- Open an item for whatever got pushed to the next version during step 1, so it doesn't quietly disappear.
- Note the release in the "Release Schedule" page if the date differs from what was originally planned there.

---

## Release Notes for Past Versions

*Owner: Developer Experience (Priya Nandakumar), later versions by Platform Tools and Docs Guild*

Every version release note gets its own page under `docs/release-notes/`. What follows is a short summary of each one shipped so far — the full writeups are the pages themselves, linked below in Related Pages.

| Version | Shipped | Owner | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1.0.0 | 2024-03-18 | Priya Nandakumar | First numbered release. Documentation described initial install steps; command help text written for the first time. |
| v1.1.0 | 2024-07-05 | Priya Nandakumar | Packaging fix — a file referenced by `MANIFEST.in` had been renamed and was missing from the distribution; documentation updated to match. |
| v1.2.0 | 2024-10-22 | Mara Olsen | Console log lines gained a timestamp prefix; before this, lines had no time information at all, which made comparing local logs to anything else nearly impossible. |
| 2.0 | 2025-02-11 | Mara Olsen | Version numbering moved from three-part to two-part starting with this release; documentation across the repo updated to match; command help text reworded for clarity. |
| 2.1 | 2025-05-27 | Sasha Perlman | Console log format changed again — fields reordered so the timestamp comes first on every line, matching the convention used elsewhere internally. Documentation updated accordingly. |
| 2.2 | 2025-09-30 | Sasha Perlman | Speed work: startup was reworked to avoid several redundant file opens, measurably shortening cold start. No documentation or format changes beyond a short note in the changelog. |

A few notes worth calling out on specific versions:

**v1.2.0** is the version most people mean when they say "before we had timestamps" — anything printed by the console before this shipped can't be reliably ordered against anything else, since lines had no time information at all.

**2.0** was a documentation-heavy release even though it also carried the numbering change; nearly every page under `docs/` got at least a small edit to reflect the new two-part version numbers.

**2.2** is the most recent version actually shipped as of this page's last update. Work toward `2.3` is in progress and tracked on the "Release Schedule" page.

---

## Files and Paths Referenced

- `accountsvc/` — the package directory itself; holds the version marker that gets updated before each release.
- `README.md` — repo-root readme with install steps and a short usage summary; kept in sync with the current version.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — repo-root changelog file, one heading per version, most recent first.
- `pyproject.toml` — packaging metadata used to build the source distribution.
- `MANIFEST.in` — lists non-code files that must be included when the distribution is built; the most common source of packaging misses when it falls out of date.
- `docs/release-notes/` — folder holding this checklist and one page per shipped version.
- `docs/console-log-format.md` — describes the expected console log line format; checked against real output during the pre-release checklist.
- `docs/cli-help-text.md` — reference copy of the current command-line help text, compared against the real printed help before each release.
- `scripts/build-sdist.sh` — convenience shell script wrapping the build and packaging-check steps.
- `dist/` — local, disposable build output folder where the source distribution file is produced; cleared before each build.
- `\\files\releases\accountsvc\` — internal file share where each version's distribution file and checksum are copied after tagging.

---

## Tools and Libraries

| Tool / package | Version | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 3.11.9 | Interpreter used to build and run the package |
| build | 1.2.1 | Produces the source distribution file from pyproject.toml |
| git | 2.43.0 | Version control and tagging releases |
| sqlite3 (command-line shell) | 3.45.1 | Opens the database file to confirm it's valid after packaging |
| tar | GNU tar 1.35 | Lists and extracts the source distribution file for inspection |
| sha256sum | GNU coreutils 9.4 | Produces a checksum alongside each distribution file |
| shellcheck | 0.9.0 | Lints the shell scripts under scripts/ |
| pandoc | 3.1.11 | Renders changelog entries into a plain-text copy for the internal wiki export |

---

## Change Log

*This section tracks changes to the checklist page itself, not to accountsvc.*

- **2024-03-10 (v1.0)** — Initial checklist assembled by Priya Nandakumar, covering the steps used for the v1.0.0 release.
- **2024-07-01 (v1.2)** — Added a packaging verification step after the v1.1.0 distribution shipped with a missing file.
- **2024-10-18 (v1.5)** — Mara Olsen added the console log format check ahead of the v1.2.0 release, once timestamps were introduced.
- **2025-02-05 (v2.0)** — Rewrote the Version Numbering section to describe the move from three-part to two-part numbers for the 2.0 release; ownership of this section moved to Platform Tools.
- **2025-09-12 (v2.2)** — Sasha Perlman folded in the current five-area grouping (documentation, packaging, help text, console log format, speed) after realizing that's all recent releases had actually contained.
- **2026-01-30 (v2.4)** — Devon Ruiz restructured the page around the Pre-Release / Packaging / Post-Release split used today, and added the Files and Tools sections.
- **2026-02-03 (v2.4)** — Small wording fixes and an updated Release Notes table following the 2.2 release.

---

## Related Pages

1	# Release Notes for v1.0.0
2	
3	**Title:** Release Notes for v1.0.0  
4	**Version:** v1.0.0  
5	**Owner:** Developer Experience (Priya Nandakumar)  
6	**Last Updated:** 2024-03-18
7	
8	## Summary
9	
10	This document covers the documentation, packaging, and command help text improvements included in v1.0.0, the first tagged build of the accountsvc package. The 1.0 release establishes baseline versioning, changelog practices, and release procedures for the team. It includes significant updates to user-facing documentation, standardization of console logging output, and initial performance optimizations in the database query layer.
11	
12	---
13	
14	## Version Numbering and Release Strategy
15	
16	*Section Owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)*
17	
18	The accountsvc package follows semantic versioning. Major version increments (e.g., 1.0 to 2.0) indicate breaking changes to the service command-line interface or database file schema. Minor versions denote backward-compatible feature additions or documentation improvements. Patch releases resolve bugs, console log formatting inconsistencies, and performance refinements without altering the service interface.
19	
20	For v1.0.0, the versioning marks the first stable release following six months of pre-release internal use. During the pre-release period, the package accumulated feedback on command-line usability, HTTP service behavior, and database file handling. The 1.0 tag signals that the package is suitable for documented internal distribution.
21	
22	The version identifier appears in:
23	- The package metadata file in the repository root
24	- Git tags in the format `v1.0.0`
25	- Release notes filenames following the pattern `release-notes-v1.0.0.md`
26	- The release schedule (version 2.5, updated 2026-04-08)
27	
28	Subsequent releases maintain this scheme: v1.1.0 for minor feature work, v1.2.0 for additional backward-compatible updates, then a jump to 2.0 when a breaking change occurs. Pre-release versions during active development use format v0.X.X.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Changelog Conventions
33	
34	*Section Owner: Docs Guild (Sasha Perlman)*
35	
36	Each release includes a dated changelog entry summarizing updates by category. The changelog conventions page (version 1.3.1, updated 2024-11-20) provides the authoritative format. The technical format specification is maintained separately in changelog-format.rst (v1.4.0, updated 2026-01-30).
37	
38	For v1.0.0, entries are organized under these headings:
39	- **Documentation:** Guide and help text improvements
40	- **Command Help Text:** Updates to the command-line interface output
41	- **Console Logging:** Changes to log message formatting and verbosity levels
42	- **Performance:** Speed and efficiency refinements in database queries
43	- **Packaging:** Changes to how the source distribution is built and distributed
44	
45	Each changelog entry under these categories includes a brief description (one to three sentences) and the contributor's name. Entries are recorded with the exact release date.
46	
47	Examples of v1.0.0 changelog entries:
48	
49	**Documentation**
50	- Rewrote the Getting Started guide to clarify database file initialization on first run and default location behavior. (Contributor: Jamie Chen)
51	- Expanded the HTTP service documentation with curl examples for common operations. (Contributor: Alex Moreno)
52	
53	**Command Help Text**
54	- Updated help text for the database path configuration flag to mention the SQLite database file location and how to override it. (Contributor: Priya Nandakumar)
55	- Clarified wording on verbosity levels in the command help output. (Contributor: Torin Vasquez)
56	
57	**Console Logging**
58	- Standardized timestamp format in console output to ISO 8601 across all log levels and contexts. (Contributor: Torin Vasquez)
59	- Adjusted logging verbosity defaults to show info-level messages without requiring flag configuration. (Contributor: Torin Vasquez)
60	
61	**Performance**
62	- Reduced database file query latency by approximately 15% through query optimization. (Contributor: Sam Liu)
63	
64	---
65	
66	## Release Checklist Process
67	
68	*Section Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*
69	
70	Before tagging a release, the team follows the release checklist (version 2.4, updated 2026-02-03). The checklist is stored in `scripts/release-checklist.md` and includes manual steps to verify code readiness, documentation completeness, and packaging correctness.
71	
72	Key checklist items for v1.0.0 were:
73	1. All new documentation pages are committed and reviewed in the `docs/` folder
74	2. Command help text is current and reflects recent feature changes
75	3. Database file schema documentation is synchronized with the actual schema
76	4. The changelog file (`docs/changelog.md`) is updated with a dated entry
77	5. The package metadata file contains the correct version string matching the intended release tag
78	6. The source distribution builds without warnings or errors
79	7. The HTTP service loopback interface responds to health checks in the built package
80	8. Console log output is verified across different verbosity settings
81	9. All documentation cross-references use correct file paths
82	10. Release notes markdown renders without syntax errors
83	
84	For v1.0.0, the release occurred on 2024-03-18 after two weeks of preparation. The checklist pass was confirmed by Mara Olsen (Platform Tools) on 2024-03-17, recorded in the project tracking system. Final confirmation to tag the release was given by Priya Nandakumar (Developer Experience) the following morning.
85	
86	The checklist serves as a gating step; a release tag is not created in the repository until all items are verified and documented in a comment on the release planning work item.
87	
88	---
89	
90	## Packaging the Source Distribution
91	
92	*Section Owner: Core Services (Elliot Fenwick)*
93	
94	The accountsvc package is distributed as a source distribution (abbreviated as sdist or tarball). Packaging details are covered comprehensively in the packaging source distribution guide (version 1.2.0, updated 2024-06-14) and supplemented by source distribution notes (version 2.1, updated 2025-08-30).
95	
96	For the v1.0.0 release, packaging steps follow this sequence:
97	
98	**1. Prepare the source tree**
99	Remove build artifacts and temporary files. Verify that `scripts/`, `docs/`, and the `accountsvc/` directory are present at the repository root. The repository structure contains no separate `src/` folder; the package directory is at the root level.
100	
101	**2. Build the distribution**
102	Run the standard Python packaging command from the repository root. The resulting tarball includes the package source, documentation files in the `docs/` folder, the root README.md, and a manifest listing all included files.
103	
104	**3. Verify contents**
105	Extract the tarball to a temporary location and confirm that all expected files are present:
106	- `docs/` folder with all markdown and rst files
107	- `accountsvc/` package directory with source modules
108	- `README.md` at the root
109	- Configuration and example files if present
110	- Scripts directory contents
111	
112	**4. Verify installation**
113	Install the package from the built tarball into an isolated environment using standard Python packaging tools. Verify that the command-line interface is accessible and the service can initialize the database file without errors.
114	
115	**5. Generate checksums**
116	Create a SHA-256 checksum file for the tarball using standard operating system utilities (Windows certutil, Linux sha256sum, or macOS shasum). The checksum file is stored alongside the tarball for checksum verification.
117	
118	**6. Upload to repository storage**
119	Place the tarball and checksum file in the `releases/` folder alongside previous release builds. Maintain a simple index listing each release filename and date.
120	
121	The v1.0.0 tarball is named `accountsvc-1.0.0.tar.gz` and measures approximately 850 KB on disk. The packaging build was performed on Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045 using standard tools available on the build machine. The tarball is compatible with extraction on Windows, Linux, and macOS systems using standard compression utilities.
122	
123	Documentation is included verbatim in the tarball under the `docs/` folder and is not transformed or compressed further during packaging.
124	
125	---
126	
127	## Release Notes and Documentation Updates
128	
129	*Section Owner: Developer Experience (Priya Nandakumar)*
130	
131	The v1.0.0 release introduced significant documentation and user interface improvements aimed at making the package more accessible to new users and clarifying edge cases discovered during the pre-release period.
132	
133	**Documentation Highlights**
134	
135	The primary documentation additions for this release include:
136	
137	- **Getting Started Guide:** A new page describing initial setup of the database file, how to verify successful initialization, configuration of the loopback HTTP service, and first interaction with the command line.
138	- **Database File Management:** Guidance on where the SQLite file is stored by default (user's local application data directory), how to relocate it to a custom path, and how to inspect its contents using standard SQLite command-line utilities.
139	- **HTTP Service Reference:** Comprehensive documentation of the loopback service interface with request-response format examples, common operations, and expected behavior.
140	- **Command-Line Reference:** Organized help documentation for all command-line flags and arguments, with realistic examples of common workflows.
141	
142	**Command Help Text Improvements**
143	
144	The command-line interface help text was substantially revised for v1.0.0. Previously, help output consisted of single-line descriptions for each flag. Starting with this release, help text for each flag includes:
145	- Clear purpose and usage context
146	- Cross-reference to the relevant documentation section
147	- Example values demonstrating realistic usage
148	- Default behavior when the flag is omitted
149	
150	For example, the help text for the database path configuration option now reads:
151	```
152	--db-path PATH
153	  Location of the SQLite database file. If not specified, the database is created
154	  in the default location ($APPDATA/accountsvc/ on Windows). See "Database File
155	  Management" in the documentation for details on custom paths and data directory
156	  structure.
157	```
158	
159	**Console Logging Format**
160	
161	Console output was standardized across all logging levels (info, warning, error). The v1.0.0 logging format includes:
162	- ISO 8601 formatted timestamp with millisecond precision
163	- Log level indicator in brackets
164	- Message text
165	- Optional context information for warnings and errors
166	
167	Example log lines:

# Release Notes for v1.0.0

**Title:** Release Notes for v1.0.0  
**Version:** v1.0.0  
**Owner:** Developer Experience (Priya Nandakumar)  
**Last Updated:** 2024-03-18

## Summary

This document covers the documentation, packaging, and command help text improvements included in v1.0.0, the first tagged build of the accountsvc package. The 1.0 release establishes baseline versioning, changelog practices, and release procedures for the team. It includes significant updates to user-facing documentation, standardization of console logging output, and initial performance optimizations in the database query layer.

---

## Version Numbering and Release Strategy

*Section Owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)*

The accountsvc package follows semantic versioning. Major version increments (e.g., 1.0 to 2.0) indicate breaking changes to the service command-line interface or database file schema. Minor versions denote backward-compatible feature additions or documentation improvements. Patch releases resolve bugs, console log formatting inconsistencies, and performance refinements without altering the service interface.

For v1.0.0, the versioning marks the first stable release following six months of pre-release internal use. During the pre-release period, the package accumulated feedback on command-line usability, HTTP service behavior, and database file handling. The 1.0 tag signals that the package is suitable for documented internal distribution.

The version identifier appears in:
- The package metadata file in the repository root
- Git tags in the format `v1.0.0`
- Release notes filenames following the pattern `release-notes-v1.0.0.md`
- The release schedule (version 2.5, updated 2026-04-08)

Subsequent releases maintain this scheme: v1.1.0 for minor feature work, v1.2.0 for additional backward-compatible updates, then a jump to 2.0 when a breaking change occurs. Pre-release versions during active development use format v0.X.X.

---

## Changelog Conventions

*Section Owner: Docs Guild (Sasha Perlman)*

Each release includes a dated changelog entry summarizing updates by category. The changelog conventions page (version 1.3.1, updated 2024-11-20) provides the authoritative format. The technical format specification is maintained separately in changelog-format.rst (v1.4.0, updated 2026-01-30).

For v1.0.0, entries are organized under these headings:
- **Documentation:** Guide and help text improvements
- **Command Help Text:** Updates to the command-line interface output
- **Console Logging:** Changes to log message formatting and verbosity levels
- **Performance:** Speed and efficiency refinements in database queries
- **Packaging:** Changes to how the source distribution is built and distributed

Each changelog entry under these categories includes a brief description (one to three sentences) and the contributor's name. Entries are recorded with the exact release date.

Examples of v1.0.0 changelog entries:

**Documentation**
- Rewrote the Getting Started guide to clarify database file initialization on first run and default location behavior. (Contributor: Jamie Chen)
- Expanded the HTTP service documentation with curl examples for common operations. (Contributor: Alex Moreno)

**Command Help Text**
- Updated help text for the database path configuration flag to mention the SQLite database file location and how to override it. (Contributor: Priya Nandakumar)
- Clarified wording on verbosity levels in the command help output. (Contributor: Torin Vasquez)

**Console Logging**
- Standardized timestamp format in console output to ISO 8601 across all log levels and contexts. (Contributor: Torin Vasquez)
- Adjusted logging verbosity defaults to show info-level messages without requiring flag configuration. (Contributor: Torin Vasquez)

**Performance**
- Reduced database file query latency by approximately 15% through query optimization. (Contributor: Sam Liu)

---

## Release Checklist Process

*Section Owner: Release Engineering (Devon Ruiz)*

Before tagging a release, the team follows the release checklist (version 2.4, updated 2026-02-03). The checklist is stored in `scripts/release-checklist.md` and includes manual steps to verify code readiness, documentation completeness, and packaging correctness.

Key checklist items for v1.0.0 were:
1. All new documentation pages are committed and reviewed in the `docs/` folder
2. Command help text is current and reflects recent feature changes
3. Database file schema documentation is synchronized with the actual schema
4. The changelog file (`docs/changelog.md`) is updated with a dated entry
5. The package metadata file contains the correct version string matching the intended release tag
6. The source distribution builds without warnings or errors
7. The HTTP service loopback interface responds to health checks in the built package
8. Console log output is verified across different verbosity settings
9. All documentation cross-references use correct file paths
10. Release notes markdown renders without syntax errors

For v1.0.0, the release occurred on 2024-03-18 after two weeks of preparation. The checklist pass was confirmed by Mara Olsen (Platform Tools) on 2024-03-17, recorded in the project tracking system. Final confirmation to tag the release was given by Priya Nandakumar (Developer Experience) the following morning.

The checklist serves as a gating step; a release tag is not created in the repository until all items are verified and documented in a comment on the release planning work item.

---

## Packaging the Source Distribution

*Section Owner: Core Services (Elliot Fenwick)*

The accountsvc package is distributed as a source distribution (abbreviated as sdist or tarball). Packaging details are covered comprehensively in the packaging source distribution guide (version 1.2.0, updated 2024-06-14) and supplemented by source distribution notes (version 2.1, updated 2025-08-30).

For the v1.0.0 release, packaging steps follow this sequence:

**1. Prepare the source tree**
Remove build artifacts and temporary files. Verify that `scripts/`, `docs/`, and the `accountsvc/` directory are present at the repository root. The repository structure contains no separate `src/` folder; the package directory is at the root level.

**2. Build the distribution**
Run the standard Python packaging command from the repository root. The resulting tarball includes the package source, documentation files in the `docs/` folder, the root README.md, and a manifest listing all included files.

**3. Verify contents**
Extract the tarball to a temporary location and confirm that all expected files are present:
- `docs/` folder with all markdown and rst files
- `accountsvc/` package directory with source modules
- `README.md` at the root
- Configuration and example files if present
- Scripts directory contents

**4. Verify installation**
Install the package from the built tarball into an isolated environment using standard Python packaging tools. Verify that the command-line interface is accessible and the service can initialize the database file without errors.

**5. Generate checksums**
Create a SHA-256 checksum file for the tarball using standard operating system utilities (Windows certutil, Linux sha256sum, or macOS shasum). The checksum file is stored alongside the tarball for checksum verification.

**6. Upload to repository storage**
Place the tarball and checksum file in the `releases/` folder alongside previous release builds. Maintain a simple index listing each release filename and date.

The v1.0.0 tarball is named `accountsvc-1.0.0.tar.gz` and measures approximately 850 KB on disk. The packaging build was performed on Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045 using standard tools available on the build machine. The tarball is compatible with extraction on Windows, Linux, and macOS systems using standard compression utilities.

Documentation is included verbatim in the tarball under the `docs/` folder and is not transformed or compressed further during packaging.

---

## Release Notes and Documentation Updates

*Section Owner: Developer Experience (Priya Nandakumar)*

The v1.0.0 release introduced significant documentation and user interface improvements aimed at making the package more accessible to new users and clarifying edge cases discovered during the pre-release period.

**Documentation Highlights**

The primary documentation additions for this release include:

- **Getting Started Guide:** A new page describing initial setup of the database file, how to verify successful initialization, configuration of the loopback HTTP service, and first interaction with the command line.
- **Database File Management:** Guidance on where the SQLite file is stored by default (user's local application data directory), how to relocate it to a custom path, and how to inspect its contents using standard SQLite command-line utilities.
- **HTTP Service Reference:** Comprehensive documentation of the loopback service interface with request-response format examples, common operations, and expected behavior.
- **Command-Line Reference:** Organized help documentation for all command-line flags and arguments, with realistic examples of common workflows.

**Command Help Text Improvements**

The command-line interface help text was substantially revised for v1.0.0. Previously, help output consisted of single-line descriptions for each flag. Starting with this release, help text for each flag includes:
- Clear purpose and usage context
- Cross-reference to the relevant documentation section
- Example values demonstrating realistic usage
- Default behavior when the flag is omitted

For example, the help text for the database path configuration option now reads:
```
--db-path PATH
  Location of the SQLite database file. If not specified, the database is created
  in the default location ($APPDATA/accountsvc/ on Windows). See "Database File
  Management" in the documentation for details on custom paths and data directory
  structure.
```

**Console Logging Format**

Console output was standardized across all logging levels (info, warning, error). The v1.0.0 logging format includes:
- ISO 8601 formatted timestamp with millisecond precision
- Log level indicator in brackets
- Message text
- Optional context information for warnings and errors

Example log lines:
```
2024-03-18T14:32:05.123Z [INFO] Service initialized on loopback interface
2024-03-18T14:32:06.456Z [WARN] Database file size approaching 100 MB
2024-03-18T14:32:07.789Z [ERROR] Failed to write account record
```

This format is consistent whether the package is run from the command line or invoked as a service. Timestamps are always in UTC to avoid timezone confusion in shared logs.

**Performance Notes**

The v1.0.0 release includes initial performance profiling and optimization. Database query latency was reduced by approximately 15% through targeted query optimization. Startup time for the service is typically under 500 milliseconds on standard hardware. These baseline metrics serve as reference points for future releases.

---

1	# Release Notes for v1.1.0
2	
3	| | |
4	|---|---|
5	| **Title** | Release Notes for v1.1.0 |
6	| **Version** | v1.1.0 |
7	| **Owner** | Developer Experience (Priya Nandakumar) |
8	| **Last updated** | 2024-07-05 |
9	
10	## Overview
11	
12	Version 1.1.0 of accountsvc focuses on packaging cleanups and standardization of console log output. This release reduces the size and complexity of the source distribution, improves cross-timezone logging consistency, and maintains full backward compatibility with existing deployments. This document covers the v1.1.0 release, release procedures applicable to the accountsvc package, and reference information for prior releases.
13	
14	For general orientation to release documentation, see the [Release Notes Folder Guide](README.md).
15	
16	## What's New in v1.1.0
17	
18	### Packaging Cleanups
19	
20	The source distribution has been streamlined by removing unused configuration file templates and build artifacts. The package now produces distributions approximately 8% smaller than v1.0.0 while retaining all necessary source code and documentation. Build metadata that was previously split across multiple configuration locations is now consolidated in a single location, making the release process more predictable and reducing errors during installation on different platforms.
21	
22	The `MANIFEST.in` file was also updated to be more explicit about which non-source files are included. This change prevents accidental inclusion of temporary files or IDE configuration that might have been present in the developer's working directory but shouldn't be distributed.
23	
24	### Console Log Format Standardization
25	
26	All diagnostic output from the service now uses ISO 8601 timestamps in the UTC timezone. Previously, the command-line tool used local system time while the loopback HTTP service used UTC, creating inconsistency when reviewing logs from different geographic regions or systems with mismatched time settings.
27	
28	The new format for all timestamps is: `2024-07-05T14:32:18Z`
29	
30	This change affects:
31	- Service startup and shutdown messages
32	- Account operation summaries (create, read, update)
33	- Database state messages
34	- Diagnostic output from the HTTP service
35	
36	While this is a minor version bump, we recognized that some users might have log parsing or alerting scripts that depend on the timestamp format. The v1.1.0 version number signals that log-dependent tooling should be reviewed and updated if needed.
37	
38	## Version Numbering Scheme
39	
40	The accountsvc package follows semantic versioning as detailed in [Version Numbering Scheme](version-numbering.md). All version numbers use the format `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, where:
41	
42	- **MAJOR** version increments for breaking changes to the service's external contracts (command-line interface, HTTP API, or database schema)
43	- **MINOR** version increments for new functionality or significant non-breaking changes (such as the logging format standardization in v1.1.0)
44	- **PATCH** version increments for bug fixes, documentation updates, and internal improvements
45	
46	In the version control system, release commits are tagged using the pattern `accountsvc-v1.1.0`. Release preparation occurs on a dedicated branch named `release/v1.1.0`, which is typically merged to the main branch after publication and then removed.
47	
48	The package metadata file (`setup.cfg`) contains the authoritative version string. During development between releases, the version string is set to a development version (e.g., `1.2.0.dev0`) to distinguish unreleased builds.
49

## Overview

Version 1.1.0 of accountsvc focuses on packaging cleanups and standardization of console log output. ## What's New in v1.1.0

### Packaging Cleanups

The source distribution has been streamlined by removing unused configuration file templates and build artifacts. The package now produces distributions approximately 8% smaller than v1.0.0 while retaining all necessary source code and documentation. Build metadata that was previously split across multiple configuration locations is now consolidated in a single location, making the release process more predictable and reducing errors during installation on different platforms.

The `MANIFEST.in` file was also updated to be more explicit about which non-source files are included. This change prevents accidental inclusion of temporary files or IDE configuration that might have been present in the developer's working directory but shouldn't be distributed.

### Console Log Format Standardization

All diagnostic output from the service now uses ISO 8601 timestamps in the UTC timezone. Previously, the command-line tool used local system time while the loopback HTTP service used UTC, creating inconsistency when reviewing logs from different geographic regions or systems with mismatched time settings.

The new format for all timestamps is: `2024-07-05T14:32:18Z`

This change affects:
- Service startup and shutdown messages
- Account operation summaries (create, read, update)
- Database state messages
- Diagnostic output from the HTTP service

While this is a minor version bump, we recognized that some users might have log parsing or alerting scripts that depend on the timestamp format. The v1.1.0 version number signals that log-dependent tooling should be reviewed and updated if needed.

## Version Numbering Scheme

The accountsvc package follows semantic versioning as detailed in [Version Numbering Scheme](version-numbering.md). All version numbers use the format `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, where:

- **MAJOR** version increments for breaking changes to the service's external contracts (command-line interface, HTTP API, or database schema)
- **MINOR** version increments for new functionality or significant non-breaking changes (such as the logging format standardization in v1.1.0)
- **PATCH** version increments for bug fixes, documentation updates, and internal improvements

In the version control system, release commits are tagged using the pattern `accountsvc-v1.1.0`. Release preparation occurs on a dedicated branch named `release/v1.1.0`, which is typically merged to the main branch after publication and then removed.

The package metadata file (`setup.cfg`) contains the authoritative version string. During development between releases, the version string is set to a development version (e.g., `1.2.0.dev0`) to distinguish unreleased builds.

A customer account managed by the service. Accounts are stored in the SQLite database file and are accessible via both the command-line tool and the HTTP service. Each account has a unique identifier and associated state information (such as creation date and account metadata).

**Loopback HTTP Service**
The built-in HTTP server provided by the accountsvc package. The service runs on the local machine and listens on a configurable port. The loopback service provides an HTTP-based alternative to the command-line tool for account operations.

**Database File**
The SQLite database file used by accountsvc to store account information. The database file is created automatically on first run and persists locally. The database file is not included in the source distribution.
