1	Title: Voice and Tone Notes
2	Version: 1.2
3	Owner: Docs Guild (Theo Banks)
4	Last updated: 2024-06-01
5	Summary: Gives short examples of preferred phrasing for describing the package's behavior in plain, calm language.
6	
7	# Voice and Tone Notes
8	
9	This page collects the working notes the Docs Guild uses when writing or reviewing pages about the package, the service, and the database file. It is the practical companion to the Writing Style Guide — this page is shorter, more example-driven, and gets updated more often because tone drifts faster than grammar rules do. If you are writing a new page or rewriting an old one and you are not sure whether a sentence "sounds like accountsvc docs," start here.
10	
11	The page also documents how tone fits into the broader documentation program: how pages get their shape from the template catalog, how new or changed terms move into the glossary, how often pages get looked at again, and how a finished page actually gets published. Those four things — style, templates, glossary, and publishing — are covered in dedicated sibling pages, but this page threads them together from the voice-and-tone angle, since tone choices usually touch all four.
12	
13	## Purpose and Coverage
14	
15	The purpose of this page is narrow on purpose: it is not a grammar reference, and it does not try to replace the Writing Style Guide. Its job is to answer the question "how do we want this to sound" with short, concrete before/after examples rather than abstract rules. Where the Writing Style Guide says "use plain language," this page shows five sentences that do and five that do not.
16	
17	In coverage:
18	
19	- word choice and sentence rhythm for describing the package, the service, and the database file
20	- tone differences between reference pages, walkthrough pages, and change logs
21	- how to write calmly about things going wrong without sounding alarmed or vague
22	- how tone choices get captured as glossary entries so they stay consistent
23	- how tone gets checked during review and during the publishing step
24	
25	Out of range for this page: page layout and required sections (see the template catalog), the mechanics of building and shipping the docs site (see the publishing workflow page), and the full list of accepted and banned terms (see the terminology reference). This page borrows examples from all three but does not restate their rules in full.
26	
27	## Voice Principles
28	
29	**Section owner: Theo Banks**
30	
31	The accountsvc docs voice has stayed fairly stable since the Docs Guild formed in late 2023. Three principles hold it together:
32	
33	1. Write like you're explaining the package to a coworker who is calm and reasonably busy, not to a stranger who needs reassurance.
34	2. Describe behavior in the present tense and in plain declarative sentences. Avoid stacking qualifiers ("generally," "in most cases," "typically") unless the behavior genuinely varies.
35	3. When something can go wrong, say what happens next in one sentence. Do not dramatize it, and do not bury it in a subordinate clause.
36	
37	A fourth, unofficial principle that shows up in review comments more than in any written rule: if a sentence needs a semicolon to hold together, it probably needs to be two sentences instead.
38	
39	None of this is about restricting vocabulary for its own sake — the terminology reference page owns the actual banned-word list — this page is about rhythm and warmth, or the deliberate lack of it. accountsvc docs are not meant to be warm. They are meant to be calm, exact, and slightly dry.
40	
41	## Tone By Content Type
42	
43	**Section owner: Theo Banks**
44	
45	Different page types earn different tone. A reference page (see the Page Template Catalog for the reference template) should read like a label: short sentences, no narrative, no "you." A walkthrough page can use "you" and can use short transitional phrases ("next," "once that's done") because a reader is following along in real time. Change log entries are the driest of all — subject, verb, object, done.
46	
47	| Page type | Voice | Example opening line |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| Reference page | Neutral, third person, no "you" | "The database file stores account state in a single local file." |
50	| Walkthrough / how-to | Second person, sequential | "Next, open the config file and confirm the local-only listener setting." |
51	| Change log entry | Terse, past tense, no adjectives | "Fixed a startup error when the database file's directory did not exist." |
52	| Troubleshooting note | Calm, cause-then-effect | "If the service does not start, check whether the port is already in use." |
53	| Glossary entry | Definitional, single sentence where possible | "Loopback service: the HTTP service the package runs, reachable only from the local host." |
54	
55	Note that troubleshooting notes are the one place where a slightly longer sentence is allowed if it keeps cause and effect in the same sentence. Splitting "if X happens" from "then Y happens" across two sentences tends to make troubleshooting text harder to scan.
56	
57	## Worked Examples: Before And After
58	
59	**Section owner: Theo Banks**
60	
61	These are pulled from real review comments (names trimmed) over the last year or so. They are meant to be copied into a review comment directly when you see the same pattern.
62	
63	* Before: "It should generally be the case that the service will typically start without issue provided that the configuration is more or less correct."
64	  After: "The service starts if the configuration file is valid."
65	
66	* Before: "Users may wish to consider potentially backing up the database file on a semi-regular basis, just to be safe."
67	  After: "Copy the database file elsewhere before making large changes to it."
68	
69	* Before: "In the event that the service fails to bind to the configured port, an error will be surfaced to the user."
70	  After: "If the port is already in use, the service prints an error and stops."
71	
72	* Before: "The package is designed in such a way as to allow for the possibility of running multiple instances."
73	  After: "You can run more than one instance of the package if each uses a different database file."
74	
75	* Before: "It is worth noting that the database file is just a regular SQLite file on disk."
76	  After: "The database file is a plain SQLite file on disk."
77	
78	A pattern worth naming out loud: "it is worth noting that" and "it should be noted that" almost never earn their place. If it's worth noting, just note it — drop the announcement.
79	
80	Two more pairs, this time about failure conditions, since that's where writers tend to either over-explain or under-explain:
81	
82	1. Before: "Should the database file become unavailable for whatever reason, the service may exhibit degraded behavior of various kinds."
83	   After: "If the database file is missing or unreadable, the service stops instead of guessing at account state."
84	
85	2. Before: "We recommend that people running this package take care to ensure the working directory is writable."
86	   After: "The package needs write access to its working directory."
87	
88	## Choosing Verbs: A Short List
89	
90	**Section owner: Theo Banks**
91	
92	A recurring source of tone drift is verb choice — writers reach for a formal-sounding verb when a plain one already does the job. This table is not comprehensive; it is the set that keeps coming up in review.
93	
94	| Instead of | Use | Why |
95	|---|---|---|
96	| "utilize" | "use" | Same meaning, fewer letters, no formality tax |
97	| "leverage" | "use" or "build on" | "Leverage" reads like a slide deck |
98	| "in order to" | "to" | Almost always drops without losing meaning |
99	| "is able to" | "can" | Shorter, same meaning |
100	| "prior to" | "before" | Plainer |
101	| "subsequent to" | "after" | Plainer |
102	| "commence" | "start" | The package starts things, it does not commence them |
103	| "terminate" | "stop" | Matches how the docs describe the service stopping |
104	| "facilitate" | "let" or "make it possible to" | "Facilitate" is vague about who does what |
105	
106	## Page Templates and Where Voice Fits In
107	
108	**Section owner: Priya Nair**
109	
110	The actual shapes of pages — required headings, front matter fields, table layouts — live in the page-template-catalog, which is owned by Priya Nair on Developer Experience (some older pages still list this as a Docs Guild property, which is out of date; the template catalog moved teams when Developer Experience formed). Voice notes do not dictate structure, but structure affects tone in one important way: templates set the reader's expectations, and tone should not fight those expectations.
111	
112	For example, the reference template opens with a one-line summary sentence before any heading. That sentence is the single hardest sentence to write calmly, because writers want to hedge it ("this page attempts to describe...") instead of just stating it ("this page describes..."). When you're filling out a template, write the summary line last, after you know what the page actually says.
113	
114	A short checklist for template + voice fit:
115	
116	- Reference pages: summary line, then definitions, no narrative voice anywhere.
117	- Walkthrough pages: numbered steps, second person, one action per step.
118	- Troubleshooting pages: symptom, then cause, then fix, in that order, every time.
119	- Change log entries: one line per entry, dated, no adjectives.
120	
121	If a template and this page's voice guidance seem to pull in different directions, the template wins on structure and this page wins on wording — raise the conflict in the weekly Docs Guild sync rather than guessing.
122	
123	## Glossary Upkeep and Tone
124	
125	**Section owner: Theo Banks**
126	
127	Every term that shows up more than twice across the docs with a specific meaning should have a glossary entry, and that entry's wording is itself a tone choice — it is usually the most-read single sentence about that term. The full process for proposing, reviewing, and merging glossary entries lives in the Glossary Upkeep Guide; this section is only about how those entries should sound.
128	
129	Glossary entries follow a fixed shape: term, colon, single definitional sentence, optional second sentence only if the first genuinely cannot stand alone. No examples inside the entry itself — examples belong on the page that uses the term, not in the glossary.
130	
131	Good entry: "Local-only listener: the setting that keeps the service reachable only from the local host and not from other machines on the network."
132	
133	Bad entry: "Local-only listener: this is basically a way of making sure that, generally speaking, other machines probably can't reach the service, which is usually what you want."
134	
135	When a new term is proposed, the person proposing it should draft the entry using the same before/after discipline as the rest of this page — write the over-explained version first if that's what comes naturally, then cut it down before submitting it for review.
136	
137	## Review Cadence and Tone Checks
138	
139	**Section owner: Mara Olsen**
140	
141	Tone is one of four things a docs review is supposed to check, alongside accuracy, template conformance, and link health. The full review schedule — who reviews what, and how often — lives on the Documentation Review Cadence page, owned by Mara Olsen on Platform Tools. From a voice standpoint, the useful part of that cadence is this: pages get a full tone pass on a fixed interval regardless of whether the underlying package changed, because tone drift happens even when nothing else does.
142	
143	The rough cadence, as of the last time this page was checked against it:
144	
145	1. Reference pages: tone-checked every quarter.
146	2. Walkthrough pages: tone-checked every quarter, content-checked whenever the package changes in a way that affects the steps.
147	3. Troubleshooting pages: tone-checked twice a year, updated as soon as a new failure mode is documented.
148	4. Change log entries: not tone-checked individually, but the change log format itself is checked against changelog-format.yaml about once a quarter.
149	
150	During a tone check, the reviewer is not trying to rewrite the page — they are trying to flag sentences that read like they were written under a deadline. A short comment ("this reads a little formal, see the before/after table on Voice and Tone Notes") is usually enough; the original author does the actual rewrite.
151	
152	## Publishing Workflow: Where Voice Gets a Last Look
153	
154	**Section owner: Mara Olsen**
155	
156	The mechanics of building and shipping the docs site — the build step, the preview step, the actual push to the internal site — are owned by Platform Tools and documented in full on the Docs Publishing Workflow page. From a tone standpoint, there is exactly one gate that matters: a page cannot go out with an open review comment tagged "tone," even if every other comment is resolved. This is enforced by convention, not by tooling, so it depends on reviewers and authors actually checking before they push.
157	
158	A short version of the relevant part of the publishing flow:
159	
160	- Draft the page against the correct template.
161	- Open the page for review; reviewers tag comments by category (tone, accuracy, structure, links).
162	- Author resolves comments, rewording per this page for anything tagged tone.
163	- Author (or a Platform Tools maintainer) runs the docs build locally to confirm the page renders.
164	- Page is merged and picked up by the next scheduled publish.
165	
166	None of this changes based on how big the change is — a one-word fix and a full rewrite go through the same gate, which sometimes annoys people fixing typos, but it keeps the tone check from becoming optional in practice.
167	
168	## Common Failure Patterns
169	
170	**Section owner: Theo Banks**
171	
172	A short, not-exhaustive list of the ways sentences drift out of tone, in rough order of how often they show up in review:
173	
174	a) Hedging that adds nothing ("may," "might," "could potentially") on behavior that is actually fixed and predictable.
175	b) Passive voice used to avoid naming what does something — "the file is written to" instead of "the package writes the file."
176	c) Reaching for a Latinate verb when a short one already exists (see the verb table above).
177	d) Explaining the same fact twice in adjacent sentences because the writer wasn't sure the first one landed.
178	e) Apologizing in text for a limitation instead of just stating it plainly.
179	
180	That last one deserves its own example. Before: "Unfortunately, the package does not currently support running against a database file on a network share, which we understand may be inconvenient for some setups." After: "The package expects the database file to be on local disk, not a network share."
181	
182	## Terminology
183	
184	The following terms are used with specific meanings throughout the docs-style pages and are worth defining here even though the full, checked list lives on the Terminology Reference page.
185	
186	- **Voice** — the consistent set of choices (formality, person, sentence length) that makes accountsvc docs sound like one team wrote them.
187	- **Tone** — the specific attitude a given sentence or page takes, which can shift by page type while staying inside the overall Voice.
188	- **Plain language** — sentence construction that avoids unnecessary formality, hedging, or Latinate substitutes for common words.
189	- **Section owner** — the person named under a heading as responsible for that section's accuracy and upkeep, not necessarily the page's overall Owner.
190	- **Front matter** — the header block at the top of a page (title, version, owner, last-updated date) described in the Page Template Catalog.
191	- **Style pass** — a review of a page focused only on wording and tone, as distinct from a content or accuracy pass.
192	- **Glossary entry** — a single defined term with its one-sentence definition, tracked per the Glossary Upkeep Guide.
193	- **Tone tag** — a review comment category used during page review to flag wording issues separately from accuracy or structure issues.
194	- **Publish gate** — the requirement that no open tone-tagged comment remain before a page is picked up by the next scheduled publish.
195	- **Loopback service** — the docs' preferred short way of referring to the package's local-only HTTP service without restating its internal mechanics on every page.
196	
197	## Files And Paths Referenced
198	
199	| Path | Purpose |
200	|---|---|
201	| docs-style/README.md | Overview of the whole docs-style folder and how its pages relate to one another. |
202	| docs-style/voice-and-tone-notes.md | This page. |
203	| docs-style/writing-style-guide.md | The full grammar and formatting rules this page's examples are meant to satisfy. |
204	| docs-style/page-template-catalog.md | Required page shapes and front matter fields for each page type. |
205	| docs-style/glossary-upkeep.md | Process for proposing, reviewing, and merging glossary entries. |
206	| docs-style/review-cadence.md | Full review schedule for all docs, including the tone-check interval referenced above. |
207	| docs-style/publishing-workflow.md | Steps for building, previewing, and pushing the docs site, including the tone publish gate. |
208	| docs-style/terminology-reference.rst | The checked, canonical list of accepted and disallowed terms. |
209	| docs-style/markdown-conventions.md | Formatting rules for markdown pages (headings, tables, code fencing). |
210	| docs-style/diagram-guidelines.md | Rules for diagrams used in walkthrough and reference pages. |
211	| docs-style/changelog-format.yaml | Machine-checked shape that change log entries must follow. |
212	| docs-style/contributor-onboarding.md | Getting-started page for anyone new to writing accountsvc docs. |
213	| docs-style/link-checking-notes.txt | Notes on how internal links are checked before publish. |
214	| docs-style/build-toolchain.rst | Details on the toolchain used to build the docs site. |
215	| docs/glossary.yml | Machine-readable mirror of the glossary entries described in Glossary Upkeep. |
216	| docs/build-logs/ | Folder holding output logs from each docs site build, used to debug failed publishes. |
217	| scripts/lint-docs.sh | Shell script that runs the prose linter against changed pages before review. |
218	| scripts/build-docs.sh | Shell script that builds the docs site locally for preview. |
219	
220	## Tools And Libraries
221	
222	| Tool | Version | Purpose |
223	|---|---|---|
224	| Vale | 3.4.1 | Prose linter that flags banned terms and some tone patterns automatically. |
225	| mkdocs | 1.6.0 | Builds the internal docs site from the markdown pages. |
226	| mkdocs-material | 9.5.3 | Theme used for the built docs site. |
227	| Pandoc | 3.1.11 | Converts the .rst pages (terminology reference, build toolchain) to previewable markdown. |
228	| markdownlint-cli | 0.41.0 | Enforces the markdown-conventions.md rules on markdown pages. |
229	| yamllint | 1.35.1 | Checks docs-style/changelog-format.yaml and docs/glossary.yml for shape errors. |
230	| Git | 2.45.0 | Version control for all docs-style pages. |
231	
232	A note on the Vale setup specifically, since it's the tool closest to this page's actual content: Vale's rule file only catches banned words and a handful of hedge phrases ("generally," "typically," "it is worth noting"). It does not catch passive voice or over-explaining — those still need a human style pass.
233	
234	## Change Log
235	
236	- 2023-11-02 — v1.0 — Initial page, shipped as part of Docs Guild release 1.0. Established the three voice principles and the first before/after table.
237	- 2024-01-15 — v1.1-draft — Added the tone-by-content-type table after review comments on the troubleshooting template kept flagging inconsistent tone. Not published as a full version bump.

Owner: Docs Guild (Theo Banks)
Last updated: 2024-06-01
Summary: Gives short examples of preferred phrasing for describing the package's behavior in plain, calm language.

# Voice and Tone Notes

This page collects the working notes the Docs Guild uses when writing or reviewing pages about the package, the service, and the database file. It is the practical companion to the Writing Style Guide — this page is shorter, more example-driven, and gets updated more often because tone drifts faster than grammar rules do. If you are writing a new page or rewriting an old one and you are not sure whether a sentence "sounds like accountsvc docs," start here.

The page also documents how tone fits into the broader documentation program: how pages get their shape from the template catalog, how new or changed terms move into the glossary, how often pages get looked at again, and how a finished page actually gets published. Those four things — style, templates, glossary, and publishing — are covered in dedicated sibling pages, but this page threads them together from the voice-and-tone angle, since tone choices usually touch all four.

## Purpose and Coverage

The purpose of this page is narrow on purpose: it is not a grammar reference, and it does not try to replace the Writing Style Guide. Its job is to answer the question "how do we want this to sound" with short, concrete before/after examples rather than abstract rules. Where the Writing Style Guide says "use plain language," this page shows five sentences that do and five that do not.

In coverage:

- word choice and sentence rhythm for describing the package, the service, and the database file
- tone differences between reference pages, walkthrough pages, and change logs
- how to write calmly about things going wrong without sounding alarmed or vague
- how tone choices get captured as glossary entries so they stay consistent
- how tone gets checked during review and during the publishing step

Out of range for this page: page layout and required sections (see the template catalog), the mechanics of building and shipping the docs site (see the publishing workflow page), and the full list of accepted and banned terms (see the terminology reference). This page borrows examples from all three but does not restate their rules in full.

## Voice Principles

**Section owner: Theo Banks**

The accountsvc docs voice has stayed fairly stable since the Docs Guild formed in late 2023. Three principles hold it together:

1. Write like you're explaining the package to a coworker who is calm and reasonably busy, not to a stranger who needs reassurance.
2. Describe behavior in the present tense and in plain declarative sentences. Avoid stacking qualifiers ("generally," "in most cases," "typically") unless the behavior genuinely varies.
3. When something can go wrong, say what happens next in one sentence. Do not dramatize it, and do not bury it in a subordinate clause.

A fourth, unofficial principle that shows up in review comments more than in any written rule: if a sentence needs a semicolon to hold together, it probably needs to be two sentences instead.

None of this is about restricting vocabulary for its own sake — the terminology reference page owns the actual banned-word list — this page is about rhythm and warmth, or the deliberate lack of it. accountsvc docs are not meant to be warm. They are meant to be calm, exact, and slightly dry.

## Tone By Content Type

**Section owner: Theo Banks**

Different page types earn different tone. A reference page (see the Page Template Catalog for the reference template) should read like a label: short sentences, no narrative, no "you." A walkthrough page can use "you" and can use short transitional phrases ("next," "once that's done") because a reader is following along in real time. Change log entries are the driest of all — subject, verb, object, done.

| Page type | Voice | Example opening line |
|---|---|---|
| Reference page | Neutral, third person, no "you" | "The database file stores account state in a single local file." |
| Walkthrough / how-to | Second person, sequential | "Next, open the config file and confirm the local-only listener setting." |
| Change log entry | Terse, past tense, no adjectives | "Fixed a startup error when the database file's directory did not exist." |
| Troubleshooting note | Calm, cause-then-effect | "If the service does not start, check whether the port is already in use." |
| Glossary entry | Definitional, single sentence where possible | "Loopback service: the HTTP service the package runs, reachable only from the local host." |

Note that troubleshooting notes are the one place where a slightly longer sentence is allowed if it keeps cause and effect in the same sentence. Splitting "if X happens" from "then Y happens" across two sentences tends to make troubleshooting text harder to scan.

## Worked Examples: Before And After

**Section owner: Theo Banks**

These are pulled from real review comments (names trimmed) over the last year or so. They are meant to be copied into a review comment directly when you see the same pattern.

* Before: "It should generally be the case that the service will typically start without issue provided that the configuration is more or less correct."
  After: "The service starts if the configuration file is valid."

* Before: "Users may wish to consider potentially backing up the database file on a semi-regular basis, just to be safe."
  After: "Copy the database file elsewhere before making large changes to it."

* Before: "In the event that the service fails to bind to the configured port, an error will be surfaced to the user."
  After: "If the port is already in use, the service prints an error and stops."

* Before: "The package is designed in such a way as to allow for the possibility of running multiple instances."
  After: "You can run more than one instance of the package if each uses a different database file."

* Before: "It is worth noting that the database file is just a regular SQLite file on disk."
  After: "The database file is a plain SQLite file on disk."

A pattern worth naming out loud: "it is worth noting that" and "it should be noted that" almost never earn their place. If it's worth noting, just note it — drop the announcement.

Two more pairs, this time about failure conditions, since that's where writers tend to either over-explain or under-explain:

1. Before: "Should the database file become unavailable for whatever reason, the service may exhibit degraded behavior of various kinds."
   After: "If the database file is missing or unreadable, the service stops instead of guessing at account state."

2. Before: "We recommend that people running this package take care to ensure the working directory is writable."
   After: "The package needs write access to its working directory."

## Choosing Verbs: A Short List

**Section owner: Theo Banks**

A recurring source of tone drift is verb choice — writers reach for a formal-sounding verb when a plain one already does the job. This table is not comprehensive; it is the set that keeps coming up in review.

| Instead of | Use | Why |
|---|---|---|
| "utilize" | "use" | Same meaning, fewer letters, no formality tax |
| "leverage" | "use" or "build on" | "Leverage" reads like a slide deck |
| "in order to" | "to" | Almost always drops without losing meaning |
| "is able to" | "can" | Shorter, same meaning |
| "prior to" | "before" | Plainer |
| "subsequent to" | "after" | Plainer |
| "commence" | "start" | The package starts things, it does not commence them |
| "terminate" | "stop" | Matches how the docs describe the service stopping |
| "facilitate" | "let" or "make it possible to" | "Facilitate" is vague about who does what |

## Page Templates and Where Voice Fits In

**Section owner: Priya Nair**

The actual shapes of pages — required headings, front matter fields, table layouts — live in the page-template-catalog, which is owned by Priya Nair on Developer Experience (some older pages still list this as a Docs Guild property, which is out of date; the template catalog moved teams when Developer Experience formed). Voice notes do not dictate structure, but structure affects tone in one important way: templates set the reader's expectations, and tone should not fight those expectations.

For example, the reference template opens with a one-line summary sentence before any heading. That sentence is the single hardest sentence to write calmly, because writers want to hedge it ("this page attempts to describe...") instead of just stating it ("this page describes..."). When you're filling out a template, write the summary line last, after you know what the page actually says.

A short checklist for template + voice fit:

- Reference pages: summary line, then definitions, no narrative voice anywhere.
- Walkthrough pages: numbered steps, second person, one action per step.
- Troubleshooting pages: symptom, then cause, then fix, in that order, every time.
- Change log entries: one line per entry, dated, no adjectives.

If a template and this page's voice guidance seem to pull in different directions, the template wins on structure and this page wins on wording — raise the conflict in the weekly Docs Guild sync rather than guessing.

## Glossary Upkeep and Tone

**Section owner: Theo Banks**

Every term that shows up more than twice across the docs with a specific meaning should have a glossary entry, and that entry's wording is itself a tone choice — it is usually the most-read single sentence about that term. The full process for proposing, reviewing, and merging glossary entries lives in the Glossary Upkeep Guide; this section is only about how those entries should sound.

Glossary entries follow a fixed shape: term, colon, single definitional sentence, optional second sentence only if the first genuinely cannot stand alone. No examples inside the entry itself — examples belong on the page that uses the term, not in the glossary.

Good entry: "Local-only listener: the setting that keeps the service reachable only from the local host and not from other machines on the network."

Bad entry: "Local-only listener: this is basically a way of making sure that, generally speaking, other machines probably can't reach the service, which is usually what you want."

When a new term is proposed, the person proposing it should draft the entry using the same before/after discipline as the rest of this page — write the over-explained version first if that's what comes naturally, then cut it down before submitting it for review.

## Review Cadence and Tone Checks

**Section owner: Mara Olsen**

Tone is one of four things a docs review is supposed to check, alongside accuracy, template conformance, and link health. The full review schedule — who reviews what, and how often — lives on the Documentation Review Cadence page, owned by Mara Olsen on Platform Tools. From a voice standpoint, the useful part of that cadence is this: pages get a full tone pass on a fixed interval regardless of whether the underlying package changed, because tone drift happens even when nothing else does.

The rough cadence, as of the last time this page was checked against it:

1. Reference pages: tone-checked every quarter.
2. Walkthrough pages: tone-checked every quarter, content-checked whenever the package changes in a way that affects the steps.
3. Troubleshooting pages: tone-checked twice a year, updated as soon as a new failure mode is documented.
4. Change log entries: not tone-checked individually, but the change log format itself is checked against changelog-format.yaml about once a quarter.

During a tone check, the reviewer is not trying to rewrite the page — they are trying to flag sentences that read like they were written under a deadline. A short comment ("this reads a little formal, see the before/after table on Voice and Tone Notes") is usually enough; the original author does the actual rewrite.

## Publishing Workflow: Where Voice Gets a Last Look

**Section owner: Mara Olsen**

The mechanics of building and shipping the docs site — the build step, the preview step, the actual push to the internal site — are owned by Platform Tools and documented in full on the Docs Publishing Workflow page. From a tone standpoint, there is exactly one gate that matters: a page cannot go out with an open review comment tagged "tone," even if every other comment is resolved. This is enforced by convention, not by tooling, so it depends on reviewers and authors actually checking before they push.

A short version of the relevant part of the publishing flow:

- Draft the page against the correct template.
- Open the page for review; reviewers tag comments by category (tone, accuracy, structure, links).
- Author resolves comments, rewording per this page for anything tagged tone.
- Author (or a Platform Tools maintainer) runs the docs build locally to confirm the page renders.
- Page is merged and picked up by the next scheduled publish.

None of this changes based on how big the change is — a one-word fix and a full rewrite go through the same gate, which sometimes annoys people fixing typos, but it keeps the tone check from becoming optional in practice.

## Common Failure Patterns

**Section owner: Theo Banks**

A short, not-exhaustive list of the ways sentences drift out of tone, in rough order of how often they show up in review:

a) Hedging that adds nothing ("may," "might," "could potentially") on behavior that is actually fixed and predictable.
b) Passive voice used to avoid naming what does something — "the file is written to" instead of "the package writes the file."
c) Reaching for a Latinate verb when a short one already exists (see the verb table above).
d) Explaining the same fact twice in adjacent sentences because the writer wasn't sure the first one landed.
e) Apologizing in text for a limitation instead of just stating it plainly.

That last one deserves its own example. Before: "Unfortunately, the package does not currently support running against a database file on a network share, which we understand may be inconvenient for some setups." After: "The package expects the database file to be on local disk, not a network share."

## Terminology

The following terms are used with specific meanings throughout the docs-style pages and are worth defining here even though the full, checked list lives on the Terminology Reference page.

- **Voice** — the consistent set of choices (formality, person, sentence length) that makes accountsvc docs sound like one team wrote them.
- **Tone** — the specific attitude a given sentence or page takes, which can shift by page type while staying inside the overall Voice.
- **Plain language** — sentence construction that avoids unnecessary formality, hedging, or Latinate substitutes for common words.
- **Section owner** — the person named under a heading as responsible for that section's accuracy and upkeep, not necessarily the page's overall Owner.
- **Front matter** — the header block at the top of a page (title, version, owner, last-updated date) described in the Page Template Catalog.
- **Style pass** — a review of a page focused only on wording and tone, as distinct from a content or accuracy pass.
- **Glossary entry** — a single defined term with its one-sentence definition, tracked per the Glossary Upkeep Guide.
- **Tone tag** — a review comment category used during page review to flag wording issues separately from accuracy or structure issues.
- **Publish gate** — the requirement that no open tone-tagged comment remain before a page is picked up by the next scheduled publish.
- **Loopback service** — the docs' preferred short way of referring to the package's local-only HTTP service without restating its internal mechanics on every page.

"""Recovery orchestration: start, complete, retry, reconcile, redrive."""
from __future__ import annotations

import secrets
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Optional

from . import mail, storage
from .delivery_address import resolve_effective_address

TOKEN_TTL = timedelta(minutes=15)
MAX_RECONCILE_RECEIPTS = 100
RECONCILABLE_STATUSES = ("delivered", "bounced", "failed")


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _expiry_from(now_iso: str) -> str:
    now = datetime.fromisoformat(now_iso)
    return (now + TOKEN_TTL).isoformat()


class RecoveryError(Exception):
    """A request-level error with an HTTP status and a stable error code."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str, status: int = 400):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code
        self.message = message
        self.status = status


class RecoveryService:
    def __init__(self, database: str, mail_endpoint: str):
        self.database = database
        self.mail_endpoint = mail_endpoint
        storage.initialize(database)

    # -- account administration -------------------------------------

    def create_account(self, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> None:
        storage.create_account(self.database, org_id, account_id, email)

    def change_email(self, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> None:
        storage.change_email(self.database, account_id, new_email)

    def show_account(self, account_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
        return storage.get_account(self.database, account_id)

    # -- recovery flow -------------------------------------------------

    def start_recovery(self, organization: str, email: str) -> dict:
        account = storage.find_account_by_email(self.database, organization, email)
        if account is None:
            # Do not reveal whether the organization/email pair exists.
            return {"request_id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "status": "accepted"}

        now = _now()
        request_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
        storage.create_recovery_request(
            self.database,
            request_id=request_id,
            org_id=organization,
            account_id=account["account_id"],
            recipient=email,
            token=token,
            created_at=now,
            expires_at=_expiry_from(now),
        )
        receipt_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        storage.create_notification(
            self.database,
            receipt_id=receipt_id,
            request_id=request_id,
            recipient=email,
            created_at=now,
        )
        status = self._attempt_delivery(receipt_id, email, token)
        return {"request_id": request_id, "status": status}

    def complete_recovery(self, token: str) -> dict:
        now = _now()
        req = storage.find_recovery_request_by_token(self.database, token)
        if req is None:
            raise RecoveryError("invalid_token", "recovery token is invalid", 400)
        if req["used_at"] is not None:
            raise RecoveryError("invalid_token", "recovery token already used", 400)
        if req["expires_at"] < now:
            raise RecoveryError("invalid_token", "recovery token has expired", 400)
        storage.mark_recovery_request_used(self.database, req["request_id"], now)
        return {
            "status": "recovered",
            "organization": req["org_id"],
            "account_id": req["account_id"],
        }

    # -- notification lifecycle -----------------------------------------

    def retry_notifications(self) -> dict:
        """Bulk-retry every notification currently marked failed."""
        failed = storage.list_notifications_by_status(self.database, "failed")
        results = []
        for notification in failed:
            req = storage.get_recovery_request(self.database, notification["request_id"])
            status = self._attempt_delivery(
                notification["receipt_id"], notification["recipient"], req["token"]
            )
            results.append({"receipt_id": notification["receipt_id"], "status": status})
        return {"retried": results}

    def redrive_notification(self, receipt_id: str) -> dict:
        """Force a resend of one specific failed notice, by its receipt id."""
        notification = storage.get_notification(self.database, receipt_id)
        if notification is None:
            raise RecoveryError("not_found", "no notification with that receipt id", 404)
        if notification["status"] != "failed":
            raise RecoveryError(
                "not_failed", "only a failed notice may be redriven", 409
            )
        req = storage.get_recovery_request(self.database, notification["request_id"])
        if req["expires_at"] < _now():
            raise RecoveryError(
                "token_expired", "the underlying recovery token has expired", 409
            )
        status = self._attempt_delivery(receipt_id, notification["recipient"], req["token"])
        return {"receipt_id": receipt_id, "status": status}

    def get_attempt_status(self, receipt_id: str) -> dict:
        """Return a notice's delivery-attempt history and its effective address."""
        notification = storage.get_notification(self.database, receipt_id)
        if notification is None:
            raise RecoveryError("not_found", "no notification with that receipt id", 404)
        req = storage.get_recovery_request(self.database, notification["request_id"])
        account = storage.get_account(self.database, req["account_id"])
        claim_history = storage.list_address_claims(self.database, req["account_id"])
        effective_address = resolve_effective_address(
            {"current_address": account["email"] if account else ""}, claim_history
        )
        return {
            "receipt_id": receipt_id,
            "status": notification["status"],
            "attempts": storage.list_attempts(self.database, receipt_id),
            "effective_address": effective_address,
        }

    def reconcile_receipts(self, receipts: list) -> dict:
        """Apply a batch of provider delivery receipts to matching notifications."""
        if not isinstance(receipts, list):
            raise RecoveryError("bad_request", "receipts must be a list", 400)
        if len(receipts) > MAX_RECONCILE_RECEIPTS:
            raise RecoveryError(
                "too_many_receipts",
                f"at most {MAX_RECONCILE_RECEIPTS} receipts per request",
                413,
            )
        now = _now()
        reconciled = []
        unknown = []
        for entry in receipts:
            receipt_id = entry.get("receipt_id") if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
            provider_status = entry.get("status") if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
            provider_message_id = (
                entry.get("provider_message_id") if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
            )
            if not receipt_id or provider_status not in RECONCILABLE_STATUSES:
                unknown.append(receipt_id)
                continue
            notification = storage.get_notification(self.database, receipt_id)
            if notification is None:
                unknown.append(receipt_id)
                continue
            storage.reconcile_notification(
                self.database,
                receipt_id=receipt_id,
                provider_status=provider_status,
                provider_message_id=provider_message_id,
                reconciled_at=now,
            )
            reconciled.append(receipt_id)
        return {"reconciled": reconciled, "unknown": unknown}

    # -- internal --------------------------------------------------------

    def _attempt_delivery(self, receipt_id: str, recipient: str, token: str) -> str:
        result = mail.send_notification(self.mail_endpoint, recipient, token, receipt_id)
        now = _now()
        storage.record_attempt(
            self.database,
            receipt_id=receipt_id,
            outcome="success" if result.success else "failure",
            http_status=result.http_status,
            error=result.error,
            attempted_at=now,
        )
        status = "sent" if result.success else "failed"
        storage.update_notification_status(self.database, receipt_id, status, now, result.error)
        return status

"""Send and retry behavior, including receipt id stability across attempts."""
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

from accountsvc import storage
from accountsvc.mail import SendResult
from accountsvc.service import RecoveryService
from tests.support import temp_database


def fake_send(results):
    """Return a stand-in for mail.send_notification that yields `results` in order."""
    calls = []

    def _send(mail_endpoint, recipient, recovery_token, receipt_id, timeout=5.0):
        calls.append(
            {
                "mail_endpoint": mail_endpoint,
                "recipient": recipient,
                "recovery_token": recovery_token,
                "receipt_id": receipt_id,
            }
        )
        outcome = results[len(calls) - 1] if len(calls) <= len(results) else results[-1]
        return outcome

    return _send, calls


class SendAndRetryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def _make_service(self, db):
        service = RecoveryService(db, mail_endpoint="http://mail.invalid/deliver")
        service.create_account("org-1", "acct-1", "user@example.com")
        return service

    def test_start_recovery_success_sends_expected_payload(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            send, calls = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None)])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")

            self.assertEqual(result["status"], "sent")
            self.assertIn("request_id", result)
            self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1)
            self.assertEqual(calls[0]["mail_endpoint"], "http://mail.invalid/deliver")
            self.assertEqual(calls[0]["recipient"], "user@example.com")
            self.assertTrue(calls[0]["recovery_token"])

    def test_start_recovery_does_not_return_secret_token(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            send, _ = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None)])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")
            self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", result)
            self.assertNotIn("token", result)

    def test_start_recovery_unknown_email_does_not_send(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            send, calls = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None)])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "nobody@example.com")
            self.assertEqual(result["status"], "accepted")
            self.assertEqual(calls, [])

    def test_failed_send_leaves_durable_failed_notification(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            send, calls = fake_send([SendResult(False, 502, "bad gateway")])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")

            self.assertEqual(result["status"], "failed")
            notifications = storage.list_notifications_by_status(db, "failed")
            self.assertEqual(len(notifications), 1)

import unittest

from accountsvc import storage
from tests.support import temp_database


class AccountStorageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_create_and_show_account(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            account = storage.get_account(db, "acct-1")
            self.assertEqual(account["org_id"], "org-1")
            self.assertEqual(account["email"], "a@example.com")

    def test_duplicate_account_id_rejected(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            with self.assertRaises(storage.AccountExistsError):
                storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "b@example.com")

    def test_duplicate_email_in_org_rejected(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            with self.assertRaises(storage.EmailInUseError):
                storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-2", "a@example.com")

    def test_same_email_allowed_across_orgs(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            storage.create_account(db, "org-2", "acct-2", "a@example.com")
            self.assertIsNotNone(storage.find_account_by_email(db, "org-2", "a@example.com"))

    def test_change_email_releases_old_address(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-2", "other@example.com")

            storage.change_email(db, "acct-1", "new@example.com")

            self.assertIsNone(storage.find_account_by_email(db, "org-1", "old@example.com"))
            self.assertIsNotNone(storage.find_account_by_email(db, "org-1", "new@example.com"))

            # Another account may now claim the released address.
            storage.change_email(db, "acct-2", "old@example.com")
            reclaimed = storage.find_account_by_email(db, "org-1", "old@example.com")
            self.assertEqual(reclaimed["account_id"], "acct-2")

    def test_change_email_conflict_raises(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-2", "b@example.com")
            with self.assertRaises(storage.EmailInUseError):
                storage.change_email(db, "acct-2", "a@example.com")

    def test_change_email_unknown_account_raises(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            with self.assertRaises(storage.AccountNotFoundError):
                storage.change_email(db, "missing", "a@example.com")

    def test_create_account_records_initial_address_claim(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")

            claims = storage.list_address_claims(db, "acct-1")
            self.assertEqual(len(claims), 1)
            self.assertEqual(claims[0]["address"], "a@example.com")
            self.assertTrue(claims[0]["claimed_at"])

    def test_change_email_appends_a_new_claim(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
            storage.change_email(db, "acct-1", "new@example.com")

            claims = storage.list_address_claims(db, "acct-1")
            self.assertEqual([c["address"] for c in claims], ["old@example.com", "new@example.com"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import unittest

from accountsvc.mail import SendResult
from accountsvc.service import RecoveryService
from tests.support import temp_database


def fake_send(results):
    """Return a stand-in for mail.send_notification that yields `results` in order."""
    calls = []

    def _send(mail_endpoint, recipient, recovery_token, receipt_id, timeout=5.0):
        calls.append(
            {
                "mail_endpoint": mail_endpoint,
                "recipient": recipient,
                "recovery_token": recovery_token,
                "receipt_id": receipt_id,
            }
        )
        outcome = results[len(calls) - 1] if len(calls) <= len(results) else results[-1]
        return outcome

    return _send, calls


class SendAndRetryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def _make_service(self, db):
        service = RecoveryService(db, mail_endpoint="http://mail.invalid/deliver")
        service.create_account("org-1", "acct-1", "user@example.com")
        return service

    def test_start_recovery_success_sends_expected_payload(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)

            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")

            self.assertEqual(result["status"], "sent")
            self.assertIn("request_id", result)
            self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1)
            self.assertEqual(calls[0]["mail_endpoint"], "http://mail.invalid/deliver")
            self.assertEqual(calls[0]["recipient"], "user@example.com")
            self.assertTrue(calls[0]["recovery_token"])

                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")
            self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", result)
            self.assertNotIn("token", result)

"""Send and retry behavior, including receipt id stability across attempts."""
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch

from accountsvc import storage
from accountsvc.mail import SendResult
from accountsvc.service import RecoveryService
from tests.support import temp_database


def fake_send(results):
    """Return a stand-in for mail.send_notification that yields `results` in order."""
    calls = []

    def _send(mail_endpoint, recipient, recovery_token, receipt_id, timeout=5.0):
        calls.append(
            {
                "mail_endpoint": mail_endpoint,
                "recipient": recipient,
                "recovery_token": recovery_token,
                "receipt_id": receipt_id,
            }
        )
        outcome = results[len(calls) - 1] if len(calls) <= len(results) else results[-1]
        return outcome

    return _send, calls


class SendAndRetryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def _make_service(self, db):
        service = RecoveryService(db, mail_endpoint="http://mail.invalid/deliver")
        service.create_account("org-1", "acct-1", "user@example.com")
        return service

    def test_start_recovery_success_sends_expected_payload(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            send, calls = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None)])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")

            self.assertEqual(result["status"], "sent")
            self.assertIn("request_id", result)
            self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1)
            self.assertEqual(calls[0]["mail_endpoint"], "http://mail.invalid/deliver")
            self.assertEqual(calls[0]["recipient"], "user@example.com")
            self.assertTrue(calls[0]["recovery_token"])

    def test_start_recovery_does_not_return_secret_token(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            send, _ = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None)])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")
            self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", result)
            self.assertNotIn("token", result)

    def test_start_recovery_unknown_email_does_not_send(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            send, calls = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None)])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "nobody@example.com")
            self.assertEqual(result["status"], "accepted")
            self.assertEqual(calls, [])

    def test_start_recovery_refuses_a_released_address(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            # acct-1 moves off user@example.com; nobody has reclaimed it.
            service.change_email("acct-1", "new@example.com")

            send, calls = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None)])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")

            self.assertEqual(result["status"], "accepted")
            self.assertEqual(calls, [])
            self.assertEqual(storage.list_notifications_by_status(db, "sent"), [])

    def test_start_recovery_for_reclaimed_address_reaches_new_owner_only(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            # acct-1 releases user@example.com; acct-2 claims it.
            service.change_email("acct-1", "new@example.com")
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-2", "user@example.com")

            send, calls = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None)])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")

            self.assertEqual(result["status"], "sent")
            self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1)
            self.assertEqual(calls[0]["recipient"], "user@example.com")

            req = storage.get_recovery_request(db, result["request_id"])
            self.assertEqual(req["account_id"], "acct-2")
            self.assertEqual(storage.get_account(db, "acct-1")["email"], "new@example.com")

    def test_failed_send_leaves_durable_failed_notification(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            send, calls = fake_send([SendResult(False, 502, "bad gateway")])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")

            self.assertEqual(result["status"], "failed")
            notifications = storage.list_notifications_by_status(db, "failed")
            self.assertEqual(len(notifications), 1)
            self.assertEqual(notifications[0]["attempt_count"], 1)
            self.assertEqual(notifications[0]["last_error"], "bad gateway")

    def test_attempts_get_a_stable_receipt_identifier(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            send, calls = fake_send([SendResult(False, 502, "bad gateway")])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                start_result = service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")

            notifications = storage.list_notifications_by_status(db, "failed")
            self.assertEqual(len(notifications), 1)
            receipt_id = notifications[0]["receipt_id"]
            self.assertTrue(receipt_id)
            self.assertEqual(calls[0]["receipt_id"], receipt_id)

            # Retrying must reuse the same receipt id rather than minting a new one.
            send2, calls2 = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None)])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send2):
                retry_result = service.retry_notifications()

            self.assertEqual(retry_result["retried"], [{"receipt_id": receipt_id, "status": "sent"}])
            self.assertEqual(calls2[0]["receipt_id"], receipt_id)

            attempts = storage.list_attempts(db, receipt_id)
            self.assertEqual([a["attempt_number"] for a in attempts], [1, 2])
            self.assertEqual([a["outcome"] for a in attempts], ["failure", "success"])

    def test_retry_only_resends_failed_notifications(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-2", "second@example.com")

            send, calls = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None), SendResult(False, 500, "boom")])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")
                service.start_recovery("org-1", "second@example.com")

            self.assertEqual(len(calls), 2)

            send2, calls2 = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None)])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send2):

                retry_result = service.retry_notifications()
            self.assertEqual(retry_result, {"retried": []})

        with temp_database() as db:

            send, calls = fake_send([SendResult(True, 200, None)])
            with patch("accountsvc.service.mail.send_notification", send):
                service.start_recovery("org-1", "user@example.com")

            result = service.complete_recovery(token)
            self.assertEqual(result["status"], "recovered")
            self.assertEqual(result["account_id"], "acct-1")

            from accountsvc.service import RecoveryError

            with self.assertRaises(RecoveryError) as ctx:
                service.complete_recovery(token)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "invalid_token")

    def test_complete_recovery_rejects_unknown_token(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            service = self._make_service(db)
            from accountsvc.service import RecoveryError

            with self.assertRaises(RecoveryError) as ctx:
                service.complete_recovery("not-a-real-token")
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "invalid_token")
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.status, 400)

import unittest

from accountsvc import storage
from tests.support import temp_database


class AccountStorageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_create_and_show_account(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            account = storage.get_account(db, "acct-1")
            self.assertEqual(account["org_id"], "org-1")
            self.assertEqual(account["email"], "a@example.com")

    def test_duplicate_account_id_rejected(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            with self.assertRaises(storage.AccountExistsError):
                storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "b@example.com")

    def test_duplicate_email_in_org_rejected(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            with self.assertRaises(storage.EmailInUseError):
                storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-2", "a@example.com")

    def test_same_email_allowed_across_orgs(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            storage.create_account(db, "org-2", "acct-2", "a@example.com")
            self.assertIsNotNone(storage.find_account_by_email(db, "org-2", "a@example.com"))

    def test_change_email_releases_old_address(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-2", "other@example.com")

            storage.change_email(db, "acct-1", "new@example.com")

            self.assertIsNone(storage.find_account_by_email(db, "org-1", "old@example.com"))
            self.assertIsNotNone(storage.find_account_by_email(db, "org-1", "new@example.com"))

            # Another account may now claim the released address.
            storage.change_email(db, "acct-2", "old@example.com")
            reclaimed = storage.find_account_by_email(db, "org-1", "old@example.com")
            self.assertEqual(reclaimed["account_id"], "acct-2")

    def test_change_email_conflict_raises(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-2", "b@example.com")
            with self.assertRaises(storage.EmailInUseError):
                storage.change_email(db, "acct-2", "a@example.com")

    def test_change_email_unknown_account_raises(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            with self.assertRaises(storage.AccountNotFoundError):
                storage.change_email(db, "missing", "a@example.com")

    def test_create_account_records_initial_address_claim(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "a@example.com")

            claims = storage.list_address_claims(db, "acct-1")
            self.assertEqual(len(claims), 1)
            self.assertEqual(claims[0]["address"], "a@example.com")
            self.assertTrue(claims[0]["claimed_at"])

    def test_change_email_appends_a_new_claim(self):
        with temp_database() as db:
            storage.create_account(db, "org-1", "acct-1", "old@example.com")
            storage.change_email(db, "acct-1", "new@example.com")

            claims = storage.list_address_claims(db, "acct-1")
            self.assertEqual([c["address"] for c in claims], ["old@example.com", "new@example.com"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Recovery orchestration: start, complete, retry, reconcile, redrive."""
from __future__ import annotations

import secrets
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from typing import Optional

from . import mail, storage
from .delivery_address import resolve_effective_address

TOKEN_TTL = timedelta(minutes=15)
MAX_RECONCILE_RECEIPTS = 100
RECONCILABLE_STATUSES = ("delivered", "bounced", "failed")


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _expiry_from(now_iso: str) -> str:
    now = datetime.fromisoformat(now_iso)
    return (now + TOKEN_TTL).isoformat()


class RecoveryError(Exception):
    """A request-level error with an HTTP status and a stable error code."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str, status: int = 400):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code
        self.message = message
        self.status = status


class RecoveryService:
    def __init__(self, database: str, mail_endpoint: str):
        self.database = database
        self.mail_endpoint = mail_endpoint
        storage.initialize(database)

    # -- account administration -------------------------------------

    def create_account(self, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> None:
        storage.create_account(self.database, org_id, account_id, email)

    def change_email(self, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> None:
        storage.change_email(self.database, account_id, new_email)

    def show_account(self, account_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
        return storage.get_account(self.database, account_id)

    # -- recovery flow -------------------------------------------------

    def start_recovery(self, organization: str, email: str) -> dict:
        account = storage.find_account_by_email(self.database, organization, email)
        if account is None:
            # Do not reveal whether the organization/email pair exists.
            return {"request_id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "status": "accepted"}

        now = _now()
        request_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
        storage.create_recovery_request(
            self.database,
            request_id=request_id,
            org_id=organization,
            account_id=account["account_id"],
            recipient=email,
            token=token,
            created_at=now,
            expires_at=_expiry_from(now),
        )
        receipt_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        storage.create_notification(
            self.database,
            receipt_id=receipt_id,
            request_id=request_id,
            recipient=email,
            created_at=now,
        )
        status = self._attempt_delivery(receipt_id, email, token)
        return {"request_id": request_id, "status": status}

    def complete_recovery(self, token: str) -> dict:
        now = _now()
        req = storage.find_recovery_request_by_token(self.database, token)
        if req is None:
            raise RecoveryError("invalid_token", "recovery token is invalid", 400)
        if req["used_at"] is not None:
            raise RecoveryError("invalid_token", "recovery token already used", 400)
        if req["expires_at"] < now:
            raise RecoveryError("invalid_token", "recovery token has expired", 400)
        storage.mark_recovery_request_used(self.database, req["request_id"], now)
        return {
            "status": "recovered",
            "organization": req["org_id"],
            "account_id": req["account_id"],
        }

    # -- notification lifecycle -----------------------------------------

    def retry_notifications(self) -> dict:
        """Bulk-retry every notification currently marked failed."""
        failed = storage.list_notifications_by_status(self.database, "failed")
        results = []
        for notification in failed:
            req = storage.get_recovery_request(self.database, notification["request_id"])
            status = self._attempt_delivery(
                notification["receipt_id"], notification["recipient"], req["token"]
            )
            results.append({"receipt_id": notification["receipt_id"], "status": status})
        return {"retried": results}

    def redrive_notification(self, receipt_id: str) -> dict:
        """Force a resend of one specific failed notice, by its receipt id."""
        notification = storage.get_notification(self.database, receipt_id)
        if notification is None:
            raise RecoveryError("not_found", "no notification with that receipt id", 404)
        if notification["status"] != "failed":
            raise RecoveryError(
                "not_failed", "only a failed notice may be redriven", 409
            )
        req = storage.get_recovery_request(self.database, notification["request_id"])
        if req["expires_at"] < _now():
            raise RecoveryError(
                "token_expired", "the underlying recovery token has expired", 409
            )
        status = self._attempt_delivery(receipt_id, notification["recipient"], req["token"])
        return {"receipt_id": receipt_id, "status": status}

    def get_attempt_status(self, receipt_id: str) -> dict:
        """Return a notice's delivery-attempt history and its effective address."""
        notification = storage.get_notification(self.database, receipt_id)
        if notification is None:
            raise RecoveryError("not_found", "no notification with that receipt id", 404)
        req = storage.get_recovery_request(self.database, notification["request_id"])
        account = storage.get_account(self.database, req["account_id"])
        claim_history = storage.list_address_claims(self.database, req["account_id"])
        effective_address = resolve_effective_address(
            {"current_address": account["email"] if account else ""}, claim_history
        )
        return {
            "receipt_id": receipt_id,
            "status": notification["status"],
            "attempts": storage.list_attempts(self.database, receipt_id),
            "effective_address": effective_address,
        }

    def reconcile_receipts(self, receipts: list) -> dict:
        """Apply a batch of provider delivery receipts to matching notifications."""
        if not isinstance(receipts, list):
            raise RecoveryError("bad_request", "receipts must be a list", 400)
        if len(receipts) > MAX_RECONCILE_RECEIPTS:
            raise RecoveryError(
                "too_many_receipts",
                f"at most {MAX_RECONCILE_RECEIPTS} receipts per request",
                413,
            )
        now = _now()
        reconciled = []
        unknown = []
        for entry in receipts:
            receipt_id = entry.get("receipt_id") if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
            provider_status = entry.get("status") if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
            provider_message_id = (
                entry.get("provider_message_id") if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
            )
            if not receipt_id or provider_status not in RECONCILABLE_STATUSES:
                unknown.append(receipt_id)
                continue
            notification = storage.get_notification(self.database, receipt_id)
            if notification is None:
                unknown.append(receipt_id)
                continue
            storage.reconcile_notification(
                self.database,
                receipt_id=receipt_id,
                provider_status=provider_status,
                provider_message_id=provider_message_id,
                reconciled_at=now,
            )
            reconciled.append(receipt_id)
        return {"reconciled": reconciled, "unknown": unknown}

    # -- internal --------------------------------------------------------

    def _attempt_delivery(self, receipt_id: str, recipient: str, token: str) -> str:
        result = mail.send_notification(self.mail_endpoint, recipient, token, receipt_id)
        now = _now()
        storage.record_attempt(
            self.database,
            receipt_id=receipt_id,
            outcome="success" if result.success else "failure",
            http_status=result.http_status,
            error=result.error,
            attempted_at=now,
        )
        status = "sent" if result.success else "failed"
        storage.update_notification_status(self.database, receipt_id, status, now, result.error)
        return status

2	"""Read-only summary of the sample display-preference records under examples/.
3	
4	Reads the JSON Lines files under examples/ (one JSON object per line) and
5	prints record counts by locale, time zone, theme, and text size, plus the
6	most common date formats, for each file and for all files combined.
7	
8	Standard library only. Reads files under examples/ only; never imports the
9	accountsvc package and never opens a database.
10	"""
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	import argparse
14	import json
15	import sys
16	from collections import Counter
17	from pathlib import Path
18	from typing import Iterable
19	
20	FIELDS = ("locale", "time_zone", "theme", "text_size")
21	DATE_FORMAT_FIELD = "date_format"
22	TOP_DATE_FORMATS = 5
23	
24	
25	class FileSummary:
26	    def __init__(self, name: str):
27	        self.name = name
28	        self.record_count = 0
29	        self.malformed_lines = 0
30	        self.counters = {field: Counter() for field in FIELDS}
31	        self.date_formats: Counter = Counter()
32	
33	    def add(self, record: dict) -> None:
34	        self.record_count += 1
35	        for field in FIELDS:
36	            value = record.get(field)
37	            if value is not None:
38	                self.counters[field][value] += 1
39	        date_format = record.get(DATE_FORMAT_FIELD)
40	        if date_format is not None:
41	            self.date_formats[date_format] += 1
42	
43	    def merge_into(self, other: "FileSummary") -> None:
44	        other.record_count += self.record_count
45	        other.malformed_lines += self.malformed_lines
46	        for field in FIELDS:
47	            other.counters[field].update(self.counters[field])
48	        other.date_formats.update(self.date_formats)
49	
50	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
51	        return {
52	            "record_count": self.record_count,
53	            "malformed_lines": self.malformed_lines,
54	            **{f"by_{field}": dict(self.counters[field].most_common()) for field in FIELDS},
55	            "most_common_date_formats": self.date_formats.most_common(TOP_DATE_FORMATS),
56	        }
57	
58	
59	def read_jsonl(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
60	    records = []
61	    malformed = 0
62	    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
63	        for line in handle:
64	            line = line.strip()
65	            if not line:
66	                continue
67	            try:
68	                obj = json.loads(line)
69	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
70	                malformed += 1
71	                continue
72	            if isinstance(obj, dict):
73	                records.append(obj)
74	            else:
75	                malformed += 1
76	    return records, malformed
77	
78	
79	def summarize_file(path: Path) -> FileSummary:
80	    summary = FileSummary(path.name)
81	    records, malformed = read_jsonl(path)
82	    summary.malformed_lines = malformed
83	    for record in records:
84	        summary.add(record)
85	    return summary
86	
87	
88	def discover_files(examples_dir: Path) -> list[Path]:
89	    return sorted(examples_dir.glob("*.jsonl"))
90	
91	
92	def combine(summaries: Iterable[FileSummary]) -> FileSummary:
93	    combined = FileSummary("ALL FILES")
94	    for summary in summaries:

96	    return combined

99	def format_counter_block(title: str, counter: Counter) -> list[str]:
100	    lines = [f"{title}:"]
101	    if not counter:
102	        lines.append("  (none)")
103	        return lines
104	    for value, count in counter.most_common():
105	        lines.append(f"  {value}: {count}")
106	    return lines

109	def format_text(name: str, summary: FileSummary) -> str:
110	    lines = [f"== {name} ==", f"records: {summary.record_count}"]
111	    if summary.malformed_lines:
112	        lines.append(f"malformed lines skipped: {summary.malformed_lines}")
113	    for field in FIELDS:

115	    lines.append("most common date formats:")

117	        lines.append("  (none)")
118	    else:
119	        for rank, (value, count) in enumerate(summary.date_formats.most_common(TOP_DATE_FORMATS), start=1):
120	            lines.append(f"  {rank}. {value}: {count}")
121	    return "\n".join(lines)

124	def resolve_target_file(examples_dir: Path, file_arg: str) -> Path:
125	    candidate = Path(file_arg)
126	    if candidate.is_file():

128	    candidate = examples_dir / file_arg

135	
136	
137	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
138	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
139	    parser.add_argument(
140	        "--examples-dir",
141	        default="examples",
142	        help="directory containing the .jsonl sample files (default: examples)",
143	    )
144	    parser.add_argument(
145	        "--file",
146	        help="summarize a single file (by name, e.g. nordics or nordics.jsonl) instead of all files",
147	    )
148	    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print machine-readable JSON instead of text")
149	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
150	
151	    examples_dir = Path(args.examples_dir)
152	
153	    if args.file:
154	        target = resolve_target_file(examples_dir, args.file)
155	        summary = summarize_file(target)
156	        if args.json:
157	            print(json.dumps({"files": {summary.name: summary.to_dict()}}, indent=2, sort_keys=False))
158	        else:
159	            print(format_text(summary.name, summary))
160	        return 0
161	
162	    if not examples_dir.is_dir():
163	        raise SystemExit(f"error: no such directory: {examples_dir}")
164	
165	    files = discover_files(examples_dir)
166	    if not files:
167	        raise SystemExit(f"error: no .jsonl files found under {examples_dir}")
168	
169	    summaries = [summarize_file(path) for path in files]
170	    combined = combine(summaries)

172	    if args.json:
173	        payload = {
174	            "files": {summary.name: summary.to_dict() for summary in summaries},
175	            "combined": combined.to_dict(),
176	        }
177	        print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=False))
178	        return 0
179	
180	    blocks = [format_text(summary.name, summary) for summary in summaries]
181	    blocks.append(format_text(f"ALL FILES ({len(files)} files)", combined))
182	    print("\n\n".join(blocks))
